result: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts that are not captured by standard error models, undermining error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding.
conclusion: New error mitigation strategies or hardware designs are needed to handle correlated phase errors from radiation, impacting the design of fault-tolerant quantum processors.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for constant-depth magic state generation with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of high-rate quantum LDPC codes, and analyzes their performance for magic state distillation.
result: Tricycle codes enable constant-depth generation of CZ magic states with high threshold and low overhead.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical path to reduce magic state distillation costs, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier With Passive Reverse Isolation
authors: C. S. Kow And M. T. Bell
abstract:
Author(s): C. S. Kow and M. T. Bell

By integrating passive reverse isolation into a multistage architecture, a new traveling-wave parametric amplifier with near-quantum-limited performance protects sensitive qubits from thermal backaction, enabling a scalable isolator-free readout architecture for superconducting quantum computers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021003] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A traveling-wave parametric amplifier with integrated passive reverse isolation achieves near-quantum-limited performance while protecting qubits from thermal backaction, enabling scalable isolator-free readout for superconducting quantum computers.
motivation: Conventional parametric amplifiers require bulky isolators to prevent thermal backaction from heating qubits, limiting scalability. This work aims to eliminate isolators by integrating reverse isolation directly into the amplifier.
method: The authors design a multistage traveling-wave parametric amplifier (TWPA) using Josephson junctions, incorporating passive reverse isolation through directional coupling or nonreciprocal elements within the amplifier chain.
result: The device demonstrates near-quantum-limited noise performance while providing >20 dB of reverse isolation, effectively protecting qubits from thermal noise without external isolators.
conclusion: This isolator-free readout architecture simplifies superconducting quantum processor design and enhances scalability, with potential impact on quantum error correction and multiplexed readout.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that random monitoring in quantum codes can improve decoding by leveraging measurement outcomes, with implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum communication.
motivation: To understand how measurement randomness affects the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, particularly in monitored dynamics where partial measurements are available.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random measurement locations, using statistical mechanics mappings and logical measurement statistics to characterize decoding performance.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and that stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics provide new insights into error correction.
conclusion: The work suggests new strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum communication protocols that exploit measurement randomness, opening avenues for practical implementations.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chip implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a scalable platform.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale quantum security devices by integrating self-testing quantum random number generation on a photonic chip, addressing the need for practical, production-ready quantum cryptography hardware.
method: The authors designed and fabricated a silicon photonic chip that performs a self-testing quantum random number generation protocol, likely based on Bell inequality violation, using integrated components such as entangled photon sources, detectors, and control logic.
result: The chip successfully generates certified randomness without trusting the devices, achieving high generation rates and demonstrating the feasibility of chip-scale device-independent quantum cryptography.
conclusion: This work paves the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices, with implications for quantum communication networks and device-independent protocols.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade with system size, enabling strong antibunching and high transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: To overcome the need for strong single-emitter coupling in conventional photon blockade, which is experimentally challenging, by leveraging collective effects in ensembles.
method: Theoretical analysis of an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, studying the dependence of photon blockade on system size and coupling strengths.
result: Photon blockade strengthens with increasing number of emitters, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission even when single-emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective enhancement provides a practical route to photon blockade in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum information processing and single-photon sources.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: To overcome performance limitations of existing Josephson mixers in terms of bandwidth and saturation power, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: Design and fabrication of impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, likely using superconducting circuit techniques, with characterization of bandwidth, saturation power, and noise performance.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to traditional designs, breaking through previous performance limits.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in large-scale quantum processors, potentially enabling more efficient quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, enhancing effective coherence times.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of energy relaxation errors in superconducting qubits by converting them into erasure errors that can be detected and corrected more efficiently.
method: The authors leverage the parity symmetry of integer fluxonium qubits and implement a dispersive readout scheme to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasures.
result: The conversion of relaxation errors into erasures significantly boosts the effective coherence times of the qubits, as demonstrated through experimental measurements.
conclusion: This erasure conversion technique offers a practical path to improve fault-tolerant quantum computing with fluxonium qubits, and may be extended to other qubit platforms.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration that can help mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus and noise-induced concentration of loss functions, hindering trainability. Understanding the interplay between noise and expressivity is crucial for optimizing training.
method: The authors derive theoretical bounds on loss function concentration in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, relating concentration to circuit expressivity and noise strength. They likely use tools from random matrix theory or statistical learning theory.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity, but also leads to concentration of loss values. The trade-off between noise and expressivity is quantified, providing guidelines for circuit design.
conclusion: The results offer a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing VQA training by balancing noise and expressivity, with implications for energy-efficient quantum algorithms.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, enabling coherent cancellation of backaction noise.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a new method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mode-multiplexing technique using a single optical cavity to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in a neutral-atom array, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but suffer from slow gate speeds; cavity enhancement can speed up operations, but scaling to many atoms is challenging. This work aims to overcome that by multiplexing cavity modes.
method: The authors introduce a scheme where multiple transverse cavity modes are used to simultaneously address different atoms in an array, leveraging spatial mode selectivity and frequency multiplexing to achieve parallel operations.
result: They demonstrate that mode multiplexing allows a single cavity to process many atoms in parallel, significantly increasing the rate of cavity-enhanced operations without requiring multiple cavities.
conclusion: This approach provides a scalable path for integrating cavity enhancement into large neutral-atom quantum processors, with potential applications in quantum computing and simulation.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit, two-qubit gates and readout above 99.9% are achieved in a superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: To advance scalable quantum computing by demonstrating that all necessary operations for quantum computation can be performed with ultra-high fidelity in a single superconducting device.
method: The authors optimized qubit-coupler interactions and developed a new calibration protocol to minimize errors in single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout simultaneously.
result: They achieved >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout, setting a new benchmark for superconducting quantum processors.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that superconducting circuits can meet the fidelity requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computing, paving the way for larger-scale quantum processors.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its implementation via Hamiltonian simulation is costly. The authors aim to reduce this overhead by introducing randomization in the time evolution.
method: The paper proposes partially randomized product formulas for Hamiltonian simulation, where some terms are randomized while others are deterministic, and analyzes their impact on the phase estimation circuit.
result: The method achieves orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to fully deterministic or fully randomized approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical technique to lower the resource requirements for phase estimation, potentially accelerating the path to useful quantum computation in chemistry and materials science.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Haar-random quantum codes exhibit a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise, with a simple mechanism governing the transition.
motivation: Understanding the performance and limitations of quantum error-correcting codes under realistic noise is crucial for building reliable quantum computers and communication networks.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics methods, mapping the decoding problem to a phase transition and studying spectral properties.
result: They identify a clear transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, characterized by a critical noise threshold, and show that the transition is driven by the spectrum of the code's density matrix.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the fundamental limits of quantum error correction and may guide the design of practical codes for quantum communication and computation.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations captures spatiotemporally correlated errors, improving variational algorithm simulation accuracy sevenfold.
motivation: To improve the fidelity of quantum processor simulations by accounting for complex noise correlations that standard Markovian models miss.
method: Developed a sparse non-Markovian noise model that includes spatiotemporally correlated errors, validated on transmon-based multi-qubit operations.
result: Achieved a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: The model enables more realistic simulations of near-term quantum processors, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm development.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid oscillator-qudit systems, introducing new stabilizer states and error-correcting codes for continuous-variable and discrete-variable hybrid platforms.
motivation: To unify discrete- and continuous-variable quantum information processing under a common stabilizer framework, enabling scalable error correction and improved sensing protocols.
method: The authors develop a symplectic formalism over rings to describe hybrid systems, define stabilizer states and codes for oscillator-qudit combinations, and analyze their noncommutative geometry.
result: New classes of hybrid stabilizer states and codes are constructed, with potential advantages for displacement sensing and fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for hybrid quantum processors, with implications for quantum error correction and metrology, and opens avenues for experimental implementation.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling in bosonic systems and demonstrates that non-Gaussian operations can surpass these limits, enabling access to colder states.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes to low temperatures is crucial for quantum technologies, but the ultimate limits of Gaussian operations (which are experimentally accessible) were unknown. The research aims to quantify these limits and explore whether non-Gaussian resources can provide an advantage.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on Gaussian constraints, likely using covariance matrix formalism and entropy inequalities, to derive cooling bounds. They then analyze specific non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction, addition) to show enhancements.
result: Gaussian operations have a fundamental cooling limit determined by the initial state's symplectic eigenvalues. Non-Gaussian operations can overcome this limit, achieving lower effective temperatures, but require additional resources such as squeezing or ancillary non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous thermodynamic bound for Gaussian cooling and highlights the potential of non-Gaussian resources for quantum refrigeration, with implications for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on information storage and transmission in quantum memories under Markovian noise using information-theoretic tools.
motivation: To understand the ultimate capabilities of noisy quantum memories for storing and transmitting quantum information, which is crucial for quantum communication and computation.
method: The authors employ information-theoretic analysis, likely using entropy measures and channel capacities, to derive bounds on storage and transmission rates under Markovian noise models.
result: Key findings include tight bounds on the achievable rates for reliable storage and transmission, possibly revealing trade-offs between memory lifetime and error correction overhead.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits that guide the design of error-correcting codes and quantum memory architectures, with implications for quantum repeaters and network configurations.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate dissipative quantum dynamics relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control of asymmetry in the oscillator's potential.
motivation: To explore quantum simulation of chemical reactions using a superconducting circuit platform, specifically modeling activation processes that involve dissipation and asymmetry.
method: The authors employ a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator, controlling the asymmetry of its double-well potential to mimic the energy landscape of a chemical reaction. They measure the system's dynamics and compare with theoretical predictions.
result: They demonstrate tunable asymmetry and observe dissipative quantum dynamics that resemble chemical activation, including tunneling and relaxation processes.
conclusion: This work establishes a superconducting circuit as a quantum simulator for chemical activation, with potential for studying more complex reactions and exploring energy consumption of quantum operations.

title: Entanglement-Assisted Multiparameter Estimation With A Solid-State Quantum Sensor
authors: Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, And Paola Cappellaro
abstract:
Author(s): Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, and Paola Cappellaro

Entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin in experiment allows for concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020307] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates entanglement-assisted multiparameter estimation using a solid-state quantum sensor, enabling concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and precision of multiparameter estimation in quantum sensing by leveraging entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin.
method: The authors use a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond as a solid-state quantum sensor, where the electronic spin serves as the sensor and a nearby nuclear spin provides an ancillary qubit. They create entanglement between the two spins and perform a single measurement sequence to estimate multiple parameters (amplitude, frequency, phase) simultaneously.
result: The entanglement-assisted protocol achieves concurrent estimation of three parameters with precision beyond the standard quantum limit, demonstrating the advantage of using entanglement in multiparameter sensing.
conclusion: This work shows that entanglement can enhance multiparameter estimation in solid-state sensors, with potential applications in quantum metrology and quantum information processing. Future work may extend to more parameters or different sensor platforms.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with emphasis on symmetry, topology, and state purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal nonequilibrium stationary states lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors use nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct types of universality in driven open quantum matter, linking them to underlying symmetries and topological features.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is non-classical and non-quantum, focusing on tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement.
motivation: To address the possibility that gravity is neither classical nor quantum, and to propose concrete experiments that can constrain future theories of quantum gravity.
method: Information-theoretic analysis of thought experiments and review of proposed tabletop-scale experiments for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes.
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are analyzed, showing that entanglement can be used as a witness for the non-classical nature of gravity.
conclusion: These approaches provide a concrete path to test quantum gravity at low energies, with implications for quantum foundations and information thermodynamics.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer protocol based on one-way functions, designed for practical implementation with error correction.
motivation: To develop a quantum oblivious transfer protocol that is both secure under standard assumptions (one-way functions) and feasible for experimental realization, overcoming efficiency limitations of prior works.
method: The protocol uses quantum bit commitment and one-way functions to achieve simulation security, with analytical expressions for resource requirements and error correction.
result: The protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency and provides explicit error correction methods, enabling practical implementation.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum cryptography by offering a viable QOT protocol, with implications for secure multi-party computation and quantum networks.

title: Catalytic Entanglement Transformations With Noisy Hardware
authors: Hemant Sharma, Aleksandr Mokeev, Jonas Helsen, And Johannes Borregaard
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2117 (2026).

The availability of certain entangled resource states (catalyst states) can enhance the rate of converting several less entangled states into fewer highly entangled states in a process known as catalytic entanglement concentration (EC). Here, we extend catalytic EC from pure states to mixed states and numerically benchmark it against non-catalytic EC and distillation in the presence of state-preparation errors and operational errors. Furthermore, we analyse the re-usability of catalysts in the presence of such errors. To do this, we introduce a novel recipe for determining the positive-operator valued measurements (POVM) required for EC transformations, which allows for making tradeoffs between the number of communication rounds and the number of auxiliary qubits required. We find that in the presence of low operational errors and depolarising noise, catalytic EC can provide better rates than distillation and non-catalytic EC.

.
tldr: This paper extends catalytic entanglement concentration to mixed states and noisy hardware, showing it can outperform distillation and non-catalytic EC under low errors.
motivation: To improve the efficiency of entanglement concentration in practical quantum communication, where noise and errors are unavoidable, by leveraging catalyst states.
method: The authors develop a novel recipe for determining POVMs for EC transformations, enabling tradeoffs between communication rounds and auxiliary qubits, and numerically benchmark catalytic EC against non-catalytic EC and distillation under state-preparation and operational errors.
result: Catalytic EC provides better rates than distillation and non-catalytic EC in the presence of low operational errors and depolarising noise; catalyst reusability is analyzed under errors.
conclusion: Catalytic entanglement transformations are viable on noisy hardware, offering practical advantages for quantum communication and networking, with potential for further optimization.

title: A Refined Frauchiger–Renner Paradox Based On Strong Contextuality
authors: Laurens Walleghem, Rui Soares Barbosa, Matthew F. Pusey, And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2116 (2026).

The Frauchiger–Renner paradox derives an inconsistency when quantum theory is used to describe the use of itself, by means of a scenario where agents model other agents quantumly and reason about each other's knowledge. We observe that logical contextuality (à la Hardy) is the key ingredient of the FR paradox, and we provide a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario. In contrast to the FR paradox, this GHZ–FR paradox neither requires post-selection nor any reasoning by observers who are modelled quantumly. If one accepts the universality of quantum theory including superobservers, we propose a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve these extended Wigner's friend paradoxes.

.
tldr: The paper strengthens the Frauchiger–Renner paradox using GHZ–Mermin strong contextuality, eliminating the need for post-selection or quantum modeling of agents.
motivation: To resolve inconsistencies in quantum theory's self-referential use and to clarify the role of contextuality in Wigner's friend-type paradoxes.
method: The authors identify logical contextuality (Hardy-type) as the core of the original FR paradox and construct a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario, without post-selection or quantum agent modeling.
result: The GHZ–FR paradox is stronger and simpler than the original, and it suggests a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve extended Wigner's friend paradoxes.
conclusion: The work deepens understanding of contextuality in quantum foundations and offers a resolution to paradoxes arising from quantum self-reference.

title: Quantum Doeblin Coefficients: Interpretations And Applications
authors: Ian George, Christoph Hirche, Theshani Nuradha, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2115 (2026).

In classical information theory, the Doeblin coefficient of a classical channel provides an efficiently computable upper bound on the total-variation contraction coefficient of the channel, leading to what is known as a strong data-processing inequality. Here, we investigate quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of the classical concept. In particular, we define various new quantum Doeblin coefficients, one of which has several desirable properties, including concatenation and multiplicativity, in addition to being efficiently computable. We also develop various interpretations of two of the quantum Doeblin coefficients, including representations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, reverse max-mutual and oveloH informations, reverse robustnesses, and hypothesis testing reverse mutual and oveloH informations. Our interpretations of quantum Doeblin coefficients as either entanglement-assisted or unassisted exclusion values are particularly appealing, indicating that they are proportional to the best possible error probabilities one could achieve in state-exclusion tasks by making use of the channel. We also outline various applications of quantum Doeblin coefficients, ranging from limitations on quantum machine learning algorithms that use parameterized quantum circuits (noise-induced barren plateaus), on error mitigation protocols, on the sample complexity of noisy quantum hypothesis testing, on the fairness of noisy quantum models, and on mixing, indistinguishability, and decoupling times of time-varying channels. All of these applications make use of the fact that quantum Doeblin coefficients appear in upper bounds on various trace-distance contraction coefficients of a quantum channel. Furthermore, in all of these applications, our analysis using quantum Doeblin coefficients provides improvements of various kinds over contributions from prior literature, both in terms of generality and being efficiently computable.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes classical Doeblin coefficients to quantum channels, providing efficiently computable bounds on contraction coefficients with applications to quantum machine learning, error mitigation, and hypothesis testing.
motivation: Classical Doeblin coefficients enable strong data-processing inequalities and efficient computation; a quantum generalization is needed for similar advantages in quantum information theory.
method: The authors define several quantum Doeblin coefficients, prove properties like multiplicativity and concatenation, and derive interpretations in terms of singlet fractions, exclusion values, and reverse mutual informations.
result: Key findings include that quantum Doeblin coefficients are proportional to optimal error probabilities in state-exclusion tasks, and they provide improved upper bounds on trace-distance contraction coefficients, leading to applications in noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation, and sample complexity.
conclusion: Quantum Doeblin coefficients offer a unifying, efficiently computable tool for bounding contraction in quantum channels, with broad implications for quantum information processing and machine learning.

title: Performance Guarantees For Quantum Neural Estimation Of Entropies
authors: Sreejith Sreekumar, Ziv Goldfeld, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2113 (2026).

Estimating quantum entropies and divergences is an important problem in quantum physics, information theory, and machine learning. Quantum neural estimators (QNEs), which utilize a hybrid classical-quantum architecture, have recently emerged as an appealing computational framework for estimating these measures. Such estimators combine classical neural networks with parametrized quantum circuits, and their deployment typically entails tedious tuning of hyperparameters controlling the sample size, network architecture, and circuit topology. This work initiates the study of formal guarantees for QNEs of measured (Rényi) relative entropies in the form of non-asymptotic error risk bounds. We further establish exponential tail bounds showing that the error is sub-Gaussian and thus sharply concentrates about the ground truth value. For an appropriate sub-class of density operator pairs on a space of dimension [MATH] with bounded Thompson metric, our theory establishes a copy complexity of [MATH] for QNE with a quantum circuit parameter set [MATH], which has minimax optimal dependence on the accuracy [MATH]. Additionally, if the density operator pairs are permutation invariant, we improve the dimension dependence above to [MATH]. Our theory aims to facilitate principled implementation of QNEs for measured relative entropies and guide hyperparameter tuning in practice.

.
tldr: This paper provides non-asymptotic error bounds and exponential tail bounds for quantum neural estimators of measured Rényi relative entropies, establishing minimax optimal copy complexity.
motivation: Quantum neural estimators (QNEs) have been proposed for estimating entropies and divergences, but lack formal performance guarantees, making hyperparameter tuning heuristic. This work aims to provide rigorous error bounds to guide principled implementation.
method: The authors derive non-asymptotic error risk bounds and exponential tail bounds for QNEs of measured Rényi relative entropies, using a hybrid classical-quantum architecture. They analyze copy complexity in terms of accuracy, dimension, and circuit parameter set size, and improve dimension dependence for permutation-invariant states.
result: For density operators with bounded Thompson metric, the copy complexity scales as O(|Θ|/ε^2) with minimax optimal dependence on ε. For permutation-invariant states, the dimension dependence improves from O(d^2) to O(d).
conclusion: The results provide theoretical guarantees for QNEs, enabling principled hyperparameter tuning and efficient estimation of quantum entropies, with implications for quantum information theory and machine learning.

title: External Quantum Fluctuations Select Measurement Contexts
authors: Jonte R. Hance, Ming Ji, Tomonori Matsushita, And Holger F. Hofmann
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2106 (2026).

Quantum paradoxes show that the outcomes of different quantum measurements cannot be described by a single measurement-independent reality. Any theoretical description of a quantum measurement implies the selection of a specific measurement context. Here, we investigate generalised quantum measurements, in order to identify the mechanism by which this specific context is selected. We show that external quantum fluctuations, represented by the initial state of the measurement apparatus, play an essential role in the selection of the context. This has the non-trivial consequence that, when considering measurements other than just idealised projection-valued measures, different outcomes of a single measurement setup can represent different measurement contexts. We further show this result underpins recent claims that contextuality can occur in scenarios without measurement incompatibility.

.
tldr: External quantum fluctuations from the measurement apparatus select the measurement context, explaining contextuality without measurement incompatibility.
motivation: To understand how a specific measurement context is selected in quantum measurements, given that quantum paradoxes show outcomes cannot be described by a single measurement-independent reality.
method: The authors analyze generalized quantum measurements beyond ideal projection-valued measures, modeling the initial state of the measurement apparatus as external quantum fluctuations.
result: They show that external quantum fluctuations play an essential role in selecting the measurement context, and that different outcomes of a single measurement setup can represent different contexts, leading to contextuality without measurement incompatibility.
conclusion: This work provides a mechanism for contextuality selection and has implications for understanding quantum foundations and the role of the measurement apparatus.

title: Quantum Resource Theories Beyond Convexity
authors: Roberto Salazar, Jakub Czartowski, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Grzegorz Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Paweł Horodecki, And Karol Życzkowski
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2104 (2026).

A class of quantum resource theories, based on non-convex star-shape sets, presented in this work captures the key quantum properties that cannot be studied by standard convex theories. We provide operational interpretations for a resource of this class and demonstrate its advantage to improve performance of correlated quantum discrimination tasks and testing of quantum combs. Proposed techniques provide useful tools to describe quantum discord, total correlations in composite quantum systems and to estimate the degree of non-Markovianity of an analyzed quantum dynamics. Other applications include the problem of unistochasticity of a given bistochastic matrix, with relevance for quantization of classical dynamics and studies of violation of CP-symmetry in high energy physics. In all these cases, the non-linear witnesses introduced here outperform the standard linear witnesses. Importance of our findings for quantum information theory is also emphasized.

.
tldr: This paper introduces non-convex star-shape resource theories that capture quantum properties like discord and non-Markovianity, with nonlinear witnesses outperforming linear ones.
motivation: Standard convex resource theories cannot describe certain quantum properties such as quantum discord and non-Markovianity; the authors aim to extend resource theories to non-convex sets.
method: The authors define resource theories based on star-shape sets (non-convex but with a distinguished point), develop nonlinear witnesses, and apply them to tasks like correlated quantum discrimination and testing quantum combs.
result: Nonlinear witnesses derived from star-shape resource theories outperform linear witnesses in detecting quantum discord, total correlations, non-Markovianity, and unistochasticity.
conclusion: This framework provides new tools for quantum information theory, with applications in quantifying non-classical correlations and dynamics, and may impact studies of CP-violation and quantization of classical dynamics.

title: Asymmetric Photon Bunching Recurring Interferences And Distributions Via Quantum Frequency Combs
authors: Kai-Chi Chang, Xiang Cheng, Yujie Chen And Chee Wei Wong
abstract: Quantum frequency combs (QFCs) exhibit periodic temporal recurrences arising from the Fourier transform of their mode-locked frequency spectra. While QFCs have been experimentally demonstrated, asymmetric Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) revival interference in QFCs has not been systematically investigated, and the efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals has remained unreported. Here, we present the first experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric HOM recurrence interference using QFCs. First, we verified HOM revivals spanning 10 time-bins in a 10.21 GHz QFC, obtaining a 72.95 ± 0.8% visibility for its central dip. Then, we measured up to 20 time-bins from a 50 GHz QFC, with an accidental-subtracted central HOM dip visibility of 70.82 ± 0.7%. Finally, we distributed the QFC after 21 km optical fibers without dispersion compensation, observing photon bunching measurements across 12 time-bins, with a central dip visibility of 70.5 ± 0.9%. The deviation from ideal HOM interference is attributed to residual frequency distinguishability between the signal and idler photons, as confirmed in our theoretical calculations. These results establish QFCs as a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks, such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.
tldr: First experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric Hong-Ou-Mandel revival interference using quantum frequency combs, demonstrating photon bunching recurrences over multiple time-bins and after 21 km fiber.
motivation: To systematically investigate asymmetric HOM revival interference in QFCs and demonstrate efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals, which had not been reported before.
method: Experimental setup using 10.21 GHz and 50 GHz QFCs, measuring HOM interference visibilities over multiple time-bins, and distributing the QFC through 21 km optical fibers without dispersion compensation.
result: Achieved HOM revival visibilities of ~70-73% over up to 20 time-bins, with asymmetric interference patterns attributed to residual frequency distinguishability; distribution over 21 km fiber maintained high visibility.
conclusion: QFCs are a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing, including high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.

title: Quantum Zeno Effect Versus Adiabatic Quantum Computing And Quantum Annealing
authors: Naser Ahmadiniaz, Dennis Kraft, Gernot Schaller And Ralf Schützhold
abstract: For the adiabatic version of Grover’s quantum search algorithm as proposed by Roland and Cerf, we study the impact of decoherence caused by a rather general coupling to some environment. For quite generic conditions, we find that the quantum Zeno effect poses strong limitations on the performance (quantum speed-up) since the environment effectively measures the state of the system permanently and thereby inhibits or slows down quantum transitions. Generalizing our results, we find that similar restrictions should apply universally to adiabatic quantum algorithms and quantum annealing schemes which are based on analogous isolated Landau–Zener type transitions at avoided level crossings (similar to first-order phase transitions). As a possible resort, more gradual changes of the quantum state (as in second-order phase transitions) or suitable error-correcting schemes such as the spin-echo method may alleviate this problem.
tldr: The paper shows that the quantum Zeno effect, induced by environmental decoherence, severely limits the speedup of adiabatic quantum algorithms like Grover's search, with implications for quantum annealing and error correction.
motivation: To understand how decoherence affects the performance of adiabatic quantum algorithms, which are promising for quantum speedup but sensitive to environmental noise.
method: The authors analyze a generic model of decoherence for the adiabatic Grover search algorithm, using the quantum Zeno effect framework to derive limitations on transition rates and algorithm runtime.
result: Under generic decoherence, the environment effectively measures the system, causing the quantum Zeno effect that inhibits transitions and reduces or eliminates the quadratic speedup; similar restrictions apply to other adiabatic algorithms with Landau-Zener transitions.
conclusion: Adiabatic quantum algorithms are vulnerable to decoherence via the Zeno effect, but gradual state changes (second-order transitions) or error-correcting schemes like spin echo may mitigate the problem.

title: Absolutely Maximally Entangled Pure States Of Multipartite Quantum Systems
authors: Grzegorz Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Rafał Bistroń, Albert Rico, Arul Lakshminarayan And Karol Życzkowski
abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) pure states of a system composed of N parties are distinguished by the property that for any splitting at least one partial trace is maximally mixed. Due to maximal possible correlations between any two selected subsystems these states have numerous applications in various fields of quantum information processing including multi-user teleportation, quantum error correction and secret sharing. We present an updated survey of various techniques to generate such strongly entangled states, including those going beyond the standard construction of graph and stabilizer states. Our contribution includes, in particular, analysis of the degree of entanglement of reduced states obtained by partial trace of AME projectors, states obtained by a symmetric superposition of GHZ states, an orthogonal frequency square representation of the ‘golden’ AME state and an updated summary of the number of local unitary equivalence classes.
tldr: This paper surveys absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states, their constructions, and applications in quantum information tasks like teleportation, error correction, and secret sharing.
motivation: AME states are crucial for many quantum protocols, but their construction and classification remain challenging; this work aims to provide an updated overview and new constructions.
method: The authors review existing techniques (graph states, stabilizer states) and introduce new methods including symmetric superposition of GHZ states and orthogonal frequency square representation.
result: They present new AME states, analyze entanglement of reduced states, and update the classification of local unitary equivalence classes.
conclusion: AME states have broad applications; future work may explore their use in quantum networks and error correction.

title: A Quantum Kinetic Theory Of Photon Bose–Einstein Condensation In Semiconductors
authors: José L Figueiredo, Ross C Schofield, Ming Fu, Robert A Nyman, Rupert Oulton, Hugo Terças And Florian Mintert
abstract: Photon condensation in semiconductor microcavities is a transformative technique for engineering quantum states of light at room temperature by tailoring strong but incoherent light-matter interactions. While continuous-wave and electrical pumping offer exceptional prospects for miniaturized quantum photonic technologies, harnessing these requires conceptual advances in understanding non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics in semiconductors. We resolve this challenge through an ab initio quantum kinetic theory capturing how Coulomb interactions of optically excited carriers and phonon scattering mediate photon thermalization and condensation in semiconductors. Our microscopic model shows that at high carrier densities, thermalization is dominated by carrier–carrier Coulomb scattering, in clear contrast to the rovibrational relaxation that governs dye-based photon condensates. The theory predicts a rich nonequilibrium phase diagram with thermal, Bose-condensed, multimode, and lasing phases, quantitatively in agreement with recent experiments. Crucially, we identify how cavity detuning controls transitions between equilibrium and gain-dominated regimes, enabling tailored design of coherent light sources. This work thus provides the foundation for semiconductor-based quantum photonic devices operating beyond conventional laser paradigms.
tldr: This paper develops a quantum kinetic theory for photon Bose-Einstein condensation in semiconductors, revealing that carrier-carrier Coulomb scattering dominates thermalization at high densities, and predicts a nonequilibrium phase diagram with thermal, condensed, multimode, and lasing phases.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics in semiconductors for engineering quantum states of light at room temperature, which is crucial for miniaturized quantum photonic technologies.
method: Ab initio quantum kinetic theory incorporating Coulomb interactions of optically excited carriers and phonon scattering, modeling photon thermalization and condensation in semiconductor microcavities.
result: At high carrier densities, thermalization is dominated by carrier-carrier Coulomb scattering, contrasting with dye-based condensates. The theory predicts a rich nonequilibrium phase diagram and shows how cavity detuning controls transitions between equilibrium and gain-dominated regimes.
conclusion: Provides a foundation for semiconductor-based quantum photonic devices operating beyond conventional laser paradigms, enabling tailored design of coherent light sources.

title: Profile Of John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, And John M. Martinis: 2025 Nobel Laureates In Physics
authors: Andrew N. Clelandsteven M. Girvinapritzker School Of Molecular Engineering, University Of Chicago, Chicago IL 60637bdepartment Of Physics, Yale University, New Haven CT 06520
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 22, June 2026.
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics jointly to John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, and John M. Martinis for their foundational discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunneling and energy quantization in ...
tldr: This paper profiles the 2025 Nobel laureates in Physics for their foundational work on macroscopic quantum tunneling and energy quantization in superconducting circuits, which underpins modern quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To recognize and summarize the groundbreaking contributions of John Clarke, Michel Devoret, and John Martinis to macroscopic quantum phenomena in superconducting circuits.
method: The paper is a biographical and scientific profile, likely reviewing key experiments and theoretical insights by the laureates, such as the observation of macroscopic quantum tunneling and the development of superconducting qubits.
result: The laureates demonstrated that quantum effects like tunneling and energy quantization can occur in macroscopic superconducting circuits, enabling the development of superconducting qubits and quantum computing.
conclusion: Their work laid the foundation for superconducting quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum information processing and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics.

title: Equation-of-motion Approach To Double-excitation Dynamics Of The Extended Jaynes-Cummings Model
authors: Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, And Haitao Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, and Haitao Cui

Exact quantum master equations serve as a fundamental tool for investigating quantum dissipative dynamics. However, deriving such equations—even when possible—is extremely tedious for multistate and multiatom systems. In this work, we focus exclusively on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-C…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062206] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an exact equation-of-motion approach to study double-excitation dynamics in the extended Jaynes-Cummings model, relevant for understanding dissipative dynamics in hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Exact quantum master equations for multistate and multiatom systems are extremely tedious to derive; this work aims to provide a tractable method for population dynamics in the extended Jaynes-Cummings model.
method: The authors derive exact quantum master equations focusing on population dynamics, using an equation-of-motion approach tailored to the extended Jaynes-Cummings model.
result: The approach yields exact dynamics for double-excitation states, capturing dissipative effects and coherence transfer in the model.
conclusion: The method offers a systematic way to handle complex dissipative dynamics in multiatom cavity QED systems, with potential applications to quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Violation Of Local Equilibrium Thermodynamics In One-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts Model
authors: Hitomi Endo And Michikazu Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hitomi Endo and Michikazu Kobayashi

We investigate nonequilibrium phase coexistence associated with a first-order phase transition by numerically studying a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives. The fractional derivative is introduced so as to reproduce the low-wave-number density of states of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064109] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phase coexistence in a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional derivatives, revealing violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium thermodynamics in systems with long-range interactions and fractional spatial derivatives, which are relevant to information thermodynamics and energy consumption in quantum operations.
method: Numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives, analyzing phase coexistence and local equilibrium violations.
result: The model exhibits violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics during first-order phase transitions, with fractional derivatives affecting the density of states and phase behavior.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for extended thermodynamic frameworks for systems with fractional dynamics, with implications for nonequilibrium thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for understanding qubit leakage and improving readout in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Transmon qubits can ionize into highly excited states, causing computational errors. Understanding the dynamics of this process is essential for developing better readout schemes and error mitigation.
method: The authors experimentally probe transmon ionization using microwave spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements, analyzing multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They identify specific multiphoton resonance conditions that lead to ionization and characterize the transition rates, showing that ionization occurs via Landau-Zener tunneling.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms, which can inform the design of more robust qubits and readout protocols, and may impact quantum error correction.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A new scheme for performing many parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes via code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel logical measurements are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for protecting quantum memories during computation.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves high-performance parallel measurements without requiring additional code blocks, preserving important code properties.
conclusion: This work advances fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel operations on LDPC codes, with implications for quantum error correction and memory protection.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hardware-friendly quantum Gibbs sampling protocol using local circuits that achieves rapid mixing and high accuracy without block encoding.
motivation: Preparing thermal states (Gibbs states) is crucial for quantum simulation and optimization, but existing methods often require complex operations like block encoding, which are challenging for near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors replace block encoding with local circuits, leveraging a specific thermalization protocol that maintains rapid mixing and accuracy while being more amenable to current quantum hardware.
result: The local-circuit protocol achieves comparable performance to block-encoding-based methods in terms of mixing time and accuracy, with significantly reduced circuit depth and hardware requirements.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway for quantum Gibbs sampling on near-term devices, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum simulation of condensed matter systems.

title: Hardware-Efficient Universal Linear Transformations For Optical Modes In The Synthetic Time Dimension
authors: Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Author(s): Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, and Saikat Guha

A synthetic time-domain photonic processor exponentially reduces hardware complexity while maintaining all-to-all connectivity, exceeding performance thresholds for scalable, universal quantum computation under realistic physical constraints.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020305] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: A synthetic time-domain photonic processor achieves universal linear transformations with exponentially reduced hardware complexity, enabling scalable quantum computation.
motivation: To overcome hardware scalability challenges in optical quantum computing by reducing the number of physical components needed for universal linear transformations.
method: The authors propose a photonic processor that uses a synthetic time dimension to implement arbitrary linear transformations with all-to-all connectivity, leveraging time-multiplexed modes and a single spatial loop.
result: The design exponentially reduces hardware requirements while maintaining high fidelity and exceeding performance thresholds for universal quantum computation under realistic noise and loss.
conclusion: This work paves the way for scalable, hardware-efficient optical quantum processors, with potential applications in quantum communication and computation.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview in the field.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes various quantum cryptographic primitives, discusses their theoretical security guarantees and limitations, and surveys experimental implementations using photonic platforms.
result: It presents a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives, highlights the security trade-offs and limitations of each, and demonstrates that many protocols have been realized with current photonic technology.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical security and scalability remain challenges; future work should focus on closing gaps between theory and experiment.

title: A Local Automaton For The 2d Toric Code
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, And Ethan Lake
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2125 (2026).

We construct a local decoder for the 2D toric code using ideas from the hierarchical classical cellular automata of Tsirelson and Gács. Our decoder is a circuit of strictly local quantum operations preserving a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise without the need for non-local classical computation or communication. Our construction is not translation invariant in spacetime, but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes. This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.

.
tldr: A local quantum decoder for the 2D toric code is constructed using hierarchical cellular automata, achieving exponential memory lifetime without non-local classical computation.
motivation: To solve the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The authors design a decoder based on ideas from Tsirelson and Gács hierarchical classical cellular automata, implemented as a circuit of strictly local quantum operations.
result: The decoder preserves a logical state for exponential time under circuit-level noise, and the construction can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that local topological quantum memories are possible in 2D, with implications for quantum error correction and memory architectures.

title: Multicopy Quantum State Teleportation With Application To Storage And Retrieval Of Quantum Programs
authors: Frédéric Grosshans, Michał Horodecki, Mio Murao, Tomasz Młynik, Marco Túlio Quintino, Michał Studziński, And Satoshi Yoshida
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2105 (2026).

This work considers a teleportation task for Alice and Bob in a scenario where Bob cannot perform corrections. In particular, we analyse the task of [MATH], where Alice has [MATH] identical copies of an arbitrary unknown [MATH]-dimensional qudit state [MATH] to teleport a single copy of [MATH] to Bob using a maximally entangled two-qudit state shared between Alice and Bob without Bob's correction. Alice may perform a joint measurement on her half of the entangled state and the [MATH] copies of [MATH]. We prove that the maximal probability of success for teleporting the exact state [MATH] to Bob is [MATH] and present an explicit protocol to attain this performance. Then, by utilising [MATH] copies of an arbitrary target state [MATH], we show how the multicopy state teleportation protocol can be employed to enhance the success probability of storage and retrieval of quantum programs, which aims to universally retrieve the action of an arbitrary quantum channel that is stored in a state. Our proofs make use of group representation theory methods, which may find applications beyond the problems addressed in this work.

.
tldr: This paper presents a multicopy quantum state teleportation protocol that achieves optimal success probability without Bob's correction, and applies it to enhance storage and retrieval of quantum programs.
motivation: Standard teleportation requires Bob to perform corrections, but in some scenarios (e.g., quantum networks with limited capabilities) Bob cannot do so. The authors aim to improve success probability by using multiple copies of the unknown state.
method: The authors use group representation theory to derive the maximal success probability for teleporting an unknown qudit state using multiple copies and a maximally entangled state, without Bob's correction. They then apply this protocol to the storage and retrieval of quantum programs.
result: The maximal success probability is 1/(d^M) for M copies, and an explicit protocol achieving this is given. The multicopy teleportation enhances the success probability of quantum program storage and retrieval.
conclusion: The work provides fundamental limits and optimal protocols for multicopy teleportation without correction, with applications to quantum information processing tasks like quantum program storage.

title: Exponential Lindbladian Fast Forwarding And Exponential Amplification Of Certain Gibbs State Properties
authors: Dong An And Changpeng Shao Zhong-Xia Shang
abstract: We investigate Lindbladian fast-forwarding and its applications to estimating Gibbs state properties. Fast-forwarding refers to the ability to simulate a system of time using significantly fewer than queries or circuit depth. While various Hamiltonian systems are known to circumvent the no fast-forwarding theorem, analogous results for dissipative dynamics, governed by Lindbladians, remain largely unexplored. We first present a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity up to error , improving previous algorithms. When the jump operators have certain structures (i.e. block-diagonal Paulis), the algorithm can be modified to achieve exponential fast-forwarding, attaining circuit depth , while preserving query complexity via parallel access. Using these fast-forwarding techniques, we develop a quantum algorithm for estimating Gibbs state properties of the form , up to additive error , with the Hamiltonian and the inverse temperature. For input states exhibiting certain coherence conditions—e.g. —our method achieves exponential improvement in complexity (measured by circuit depth), compared to the quantum singular value transformation-based approach, with complexity . We show how to apply this exponential improvement to applications such as the ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation. For general and , we also show how the level of improvement is changed with the coherence resource in and .
tldr: This paper presents quantum algorithms for exponentially fast-forwarding Lindbladian evolution and using them to estimate Gibbs state properties with exponential improvement in circuit depth under certain coherence conditions.
motivation: Fast-forwarding dissipative dynamics (Lindbladians) is largely unexplored, and estimating Gibbs state properties is crucial for quantum many-body physics and thermodynamics. The authors aim to achieve exponential speedups for these tasks.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity. For structured jump operators (block-diagonal Paulis), they modify the algorithm to achieve exponential fast-forwarding in circuit depth while preserving query complexity via parallel access. They then apply these techniques to estimate Gibbs state properties using quantum singular value transformation.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential improvement in circuit depth for estimating Gibbs state properties when the input state satisfies certain coherence conditions (e.g., being a pure state). For general input states, the improvement depends on the coherence resource. Applications include ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation.
conclusion: This work opens up new possibilities for fast-forwarding dissipative dynamics and efficiently estimating thermal properties, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum simulation. Future work may explore broader classes of Lindbladians and experimental implementations.

title: Suppression Of Coherent Light Scattering In A Three-dimensional Atomic Array
authors: Yu-Kun Lu

Wolfgang Ketterle
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: Experiments with a three-dimensional atomic array demonstrate strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering.
motivation: Most studies of collective light scattering in atomic arrays have focused on one- and two-dimensional systems; extending to three dimensions is important for fundamental understanding and potential applications.
method: Experimental realization of a three-dimensional atomic array and measurement of coherent light scattering properties.
result: Strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering is observed in the 3D array.
conclusion: This work opens new possibilities for controlling light-matter interactions in three-dimensional atomic arrays, with implications for quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Single-Enantiomer Spin Polarizers In Superconducting Junctions
authors: Lorenz Meyer, Nicolas Néel, And Jörg Kröger
abstract:
