A new experiment shows that spin-polarized currents conducted by helical organic molecules are not just a measurement artifact, as some researchers suspected.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226201] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that spin-polarized currents in superconducting junctions using helical organic molecules are real and not artifacts, with implications for hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To resolve controversy about whether spin-polarized currents from helical molecules are genuine or measurement artifacts, and to explore their potential in superconducting spintronics.
method: Experimental measurement of spin-polarized transport in superconducting junctions incorporating helical organic molecules as spin filters.
result: Confirmed that single-enantiomer helical molecules produce spin-polarized currents in superconducting junctions, ruling out artifact explanations.
conclusion: Validates the use of chiral molecules for spin polarization in superconducting circuits, opening avenues for hybrid quantum systems combining molecular spintronics with superconductivity.

title: Impact Of The Unruh Effect On The Estimation Precision Of Gaussian Channel Parameters
authors: Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, And Xingdong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, and Xingdong Zhao

Gaussian quantum channels constitute a pivotal physical framework for characterizing the dynamics of Gaussian quantum states. Extensive scholarly attention has been devoted to the estimation of parameters associated with Gaussian channels. However, while previous research has predominantly focused o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062609] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how the Unruh effect degrades the estimation precision of Gaussian channel parameters, relevant for quantum communication in relativistic settings.
motivation: Previous work on Gaussian channel estimation ignored relativistic effects like the Unruh effect, which can impact precision in scenarios involving accelerated observers or black holes.
method: The authors model a Gaussian channel under the influence of the Unruh effect using a uniformly accelerated observer and analyze the quantum Fisher information for parameter estimation.
result: The Unruh effect reduces the estimation precision, with the degradation depending on the acceleration parameter and the channel parameters.
conclusion: Relativistic effects must be considered for precise quantum metrology in non-inertial frames, and the results may inform quantum communication protocols in curved spacetime.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, and Ujjwal Sen

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares the performance of PPT and moment-based entanglement detection criteria under detection loophole conditions, finding that PPT remains more robust.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies, but real-world detectors have inefficiencies (detection loophole) that can affect the reliability of detection criteria. The study aims to understand how this loophole impacts two major detection methods.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and compare the positive partial transposition (PPT) criterion and moment-based criteria for entanglement detection, incorporating a detection loophole model where detectors have finite efficiency.
result: Under the detection loophole, the PPT criterion outperforms moment-based criteria, detecting a larger set of entangled states. The advantage persists even for low detection efficiencies.
conclusion: The findings guide experimentalists in choosing robust entanglement detection methods for practical quantum communication and computation, and highlight the need for loophole-resistant certification techniques.

title: Hamiltonian Simulation With Explicit Formulas For Digital-analog Quantum Computing
authors: Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, And Gonzalo Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, and Gonzalo Camacho

Digital-analog is a quantum computational paradigm that employs the natural interaction Hamiltonian of a system as the entangling resource, combined with single qubit gates, to implement universal quantum operations. As in the case of its digital gate-based counterpart, designing digital-analog circ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062607] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in digital-analog quantum computing, leveraging natural interaction Hamiltonians as entangling resources.
motivation: Digital-analog quantum computing offers a promising paradigm that combines the flexibility of digital gates with the efficiency of analog interactions, but systematic methods for simulating arbitrary Hamiltonians are lacking.
method: The authors derive explicit analytical formulas for decomposing target Hamiltonians into sequences of single-qubit gates and the system's natural interaction Hamiltonian, using Trotterization and commutator expansions.
result: They provide closed-form expressions for the required gate sequences and durations, enabling efficient simulation of a wide class of Hamiltonians with reduced gate overhead compared to fully digital approaches.
conclusion: The work advances the practical implementation of digital-analog quantum computing by providing a systematic framework for Hamiltonian simulation, with potential applications in quantum simulation and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Non-Clifford Quantum Gate Teleportation With Generalized Lattice Surgery
authors: Yifei Wang And Yingfei Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Wang and Yingfei Gu

We propose a distillation-free scheme for the fault‐tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level, thereby completing the universal gate set. Our approach exploits generalized lattice surgery to integrate two quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. Specifically, non-Clifford gates…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062410] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a distillation-free scheme for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates using generalized lattice surgery to integrate two QEC codes.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computation requires non-Clifford gates, which are typically resource-intensive due to distillation. This work aims to reduce overhead by eliminating distillation.
method: Generalized lattice surgery is used to combine two quantum error-correcting codes, enabling the direct implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level without state distillation.
result: The scheme achieves fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates with reduced resource overhead compared to traditional distillation-based methods.
conclusion: This approach simplifies the implementation of universal gate sets in fault-tolerant quantum computing, potentially accelerating practical quantum computation.

title: Time-optimal Control Of A ${\mathrm{GdW}}_{30}$ Molecular Spin Qudit
authors: Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, And Josep Maria Bofill
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, and Josep Maria Bofill

Quantum systems with more than two levels, known as qudits, offer enhanced information density and potentially more efficient quantum operations compared with traditional qubits. Among the various physical platforms under investigation, single-molecule magnets (SMMs) stand out due to their intrinsic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062603] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates time-optimal control of a GdW30 molecular spin qudit, achieving fast and high-fidelity quantum operations.
motivation: To exploit the larger Hilbert space of qudits for more efficient quantum information processing, and to demonstrate control on a molecular spin platform.
method: The authors use optimal control theory (GRAPE algorithm) to design microwave pulses that implement arbitrary unitary operations on the 7-level spin qudit of GdW30.
result: They achieve gate fidelities above 99% with operation times on the order of tens of nanoseconds, showing that molecular spin qudits can be controlled with high speed and accuracy.
conclusion: Molecular spin qudits are a promising platform for quantum computing, and optimal control can mitigate errors from inhomogeneous broadening and other decoherence sources.

title: Bosonic Holes In Quadratic Bosonic Systems
authors: Jia-Ming Hu, Bo Wang, And Ze-Liang Xiang
abstract:

Hole degrees of freedom play a central role in the exact solution of quadratic (mean-field) systems. Although a variety of experiments have suggested the existence of bosonic holes, a consistent and complete theory has long been hindered by the ghost problems. Here, we resolve the ghost problem and …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224305] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper resolves the ghost problem in quadratic bosonic systems and provides a consistent theory of bosonic holes.
motivation: Bosonic holes are important for exact solutions of quadratic systems, but a complete theory was hindered by ghost problems. This work aims to resolve that.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to eliminate ghost states and define bosonic hole degrees of freedom consistently.
result: They successfully resolve the ghost problem and establish a consistent theory of bosonic holes in quadratic bosonic systems.
conclusion: The results provide a foundation for understanding bosonic holes, with potential applications in hybrid quantum systems and condensed matter physics.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder

motivation: Understanding phononic properties of SnV centers is crucial for their use in quantum technologies, as phonons affect coherence and spin dynamics.
method: Optical spectroscopy and coherent population trapping experiments were performed on SnV centers in diamond to measure linewidth broadening and ground-state orbital level coherence.
result: The study reveals phonon-induced linewidth broadening and demonstrates CPT between ground-state orbital levels, providing insight into the phononic environment.
conclusion: These findings help optimize SnV centers for quantum applications, such as quantum repeaters and transducers, by informing strategies to mitigate phonon decoherence.

title: Constant Geometric Speed Schedule For Adiabatic State Preparation
authors: Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, And Sangkook Choi

The efficiency of adiabatic quantum evolution is governed by the evolution time [MATH], which typically scales as [MATH] with the minimum energy gap [MATH]. However, the rigorous lower bound is [MATH], where [MATH] is the adiabatic path length. Al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023233] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a constant geometric speed schedule for adiabatic state preparation that minimizes the evolution time by maintaining a constant speed along the adiabatic path, achieving the rigorous lower bound.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum evolution is limited by the minimum energy gap, leading to long evolution times. The authors aim to optimize the schedule to achieve the theoretical lower bound on evolution time.
method: The authors derive a schedule that keeps the geometric speed constant along the adiabatic path, using the concept of adiabatic path length and the quantum geometric tensor.
result: The constant geometric speed schedule achieves the rigorous lower bound on evolution time, scaling as the square of the path length, and outperforms traditional linear schedules.
conclusion: This work provides an optimal scheduling strategy for adiabatic state preparation, with implications for quantum computing and quantum simulation, potentially reducing resource requirements.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity sufficient to constrain topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: To understand the entropy contributions from spin and orbital degrees of freedom in strongly correlated electron systems, and to assess the feasibility of isolating topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum Hall states.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a local thermometer in a two-dimensional electron gas in a partially filled Landau level, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: Observed successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom as temperature decreases, with entropy steps corresponding to known phase transitions; achieved sensitivity that can constrain topological entropy in non-Abelian states.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a thermodynamic probe of quantum Hall phases and provides a pathway to detect topological order via entropy measurements.

method: Time-resolved noise thermometry was used to measure the temperature evolution of mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse.
result: A two-step thermalization process was observed, attributed to the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into energy dissipation and thermalization in mesoscopic systems, with implications for quantum device design and information thermodynamics.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements

[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readouts of qubit states to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, providing a more complete picture of the noise environment affecting qubits.
conclusion: This technique enhances noise characterization for qubit systems, which is important for improving qubit performance and understanding decoherence mechanisms. It may be applied to various qubit platforms.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout

motivation: To identify and characterize a solid-state spin defect in a wide-band-gap oxide that can serve as a scalable quantum platform with long coherence and efficient readout.

result: Discovery of a deep-level defect in ZnO with 4-ms spin coherence time, small electron-phonon coupling, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO defects are a promising new platform for scalable quantum technologies, with potential for quantum sensing, communication, and computing.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. motivation: Quantum nondemolition measurements are crucial for quantum error correction and communication, but multilevel systems suffer from measurement-induced errors. This work aims to improve readout fidelity while preserving quantum states.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize back-action on the qudit state.
result: The protocol achieves 99.61% readout fidelity with reduced measurement time and significantly mitigates measurement-induced errors across different quantum platforms.
conclusion: This adaptive readout technique enhances the nondemolition nature of measurements, which is beneficial for quantum error correction and quantum communication protocols that rely on high-fidelity state readout.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method identifies the most strongly squeezed supermodes in multimode squeezed light, enabling compression of photonic processors from quadratic to near-constant hardware footprint.
motivation: Multimode squeezed light is a key resource for quantum information processing, but processing it typically requires hardware that scales quadratically with the number of modes. This work aims to reduce that overhead.
method: The authors use a variational approach to find the supermodes (linear combinations of original modes) that carry the most squeezing, effectively compressing the relevant information into a smaller number of modes.
result: They demonstrate that the number of relevant supermodes is nearly constant, independent of the total number of modes, leading to a dramatic reduction in hardware requirements for multimode photonic processors.
conclusion: This variational compression technique could enable scalable quantum information processing with squeezed light, with potential applications in quantum computing, communication, and sensing.

title: Overhead In Quantum Circuits With Time-Multiplexed Qubit Control
authors: Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, And Anton Frisk Kockum

Scaling quantum processors via shared control lines is more efficient than expected, with serialization costs scaling only logarithmically and posing no overhead for certain two-qubit gate configurations.

tldr: This paper shows that time-multiplexed qubit control via shared lines incurs only logarithmic overhead, making it efficient for scaling quantum processors.
motivation: Scaling quantum processors requires many control lines, which is challenging. The authors investigate whether time-multiplexed control can reduce hardware overhead without significant performance penalties.
method: The authors analyze the overhead of serializing control pulses for qubits sharing a control line, considering different two-qubit gate configurations and using theoretical scaling arguments.
result: The overhead scales logarithmically with the number of qubits, and for certain two-qubit gate configurations, there is no overhead at all.
conclusion: Time-multiplexed control is a viable strategy for scaling quantum processors, with implications for reducing wiring complexity in superconducting circuits and other platforms.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of A Two-voter Quantum Anonymous Voting Prototype With Continuous Variables
authors: Piao Tan

motivation: Anonymous voting is a fundamental cryptographic task; quantum protocols can provide information-theoretic security. This work aims to realize such a protocol experimentally with continuous variables, which are more practical than discrete-variable implementations.
method: The authors implement a two-voter quantum anonymous voting scheme using continuous-variable quantum states (likely coherent states or squeezed states) and homodyne detection. The protocol ensures voter anonymity and verifiability.
result: The experimental prototype successfully demonstrates anonymous voting with two voters, achieving security against certain attacks and showing feasibility of continuous-variable quantum anonymous voting.
conclusion: This work provides a proof-of-principle for continuous-variable quantum anonymous voting, paving the way for scalable quantum network applications. Future work may extend to more voters and integrate with quantum repeaters.

title: Graph-theoretic Quantum Contextuality And Unextendible Product Bases

Unextendible product bases (UPBs) are central to the study of local distinguishability of orthogonal product states. While their connection to quantum nonlocality via Bell inequalities is well established, their link to quantum contextuality remains largely unexplored. We establish a graph theoretic…

tldr: This paper establishes a graph-theoretic connection between unextendible product bases (UPBs) and quantum contextuality, showing that UPBs can be used to construct contextuality proofs.
motivation: While UPBs are known to be related to nonlocality, their connection to contextuality was unexplored. The authors aim to bridge this gap using graph theory.
method: The authors use graph-theoretic methods, specifically the exclusivity graph approach, to analyze UPBs and derive contextuality inequalities.
result: They show that certain UPBs correspond to noncontextuality inequalities that are violated by quantum mechanics, thus linking UPBs to contextuality.
conclusion: This work provides a new perspective on UPBs and contextuality, potentially leading to new insights in quantum foundations and quantum information.

Spin-triplet superconductors are promising platforms for dissipationless spin transport, which typically originates from the interplay of ferromagnetism and superconductivity. However, ferromagnetism, in turn, suppresses superconductivity. As a class of unconventional magnetic materials, [MATH]-wave ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214511] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates spin-triplet pairing and spin supercurrent in p-wave magnetic superconductors, offering a platform for dissipationless spin transport.
motivation: Spin-triplet superconductors are promising for dissipationless spin transport, but ferromagnetism typically suppresses superconductivity. The authors aim to explore p-wave magnetic superconductors as a way to achieve spin-triplet pairing without strong ferromagnetic suppression.
method: The study uses theoretical modeling and analysis of p-wave magnetic superconductors, likely employing mean-field theory or Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations to investigate pairing symmetry and supercurrent.
result: They find that p-wave magnetic superconductors can host spin-triplet pairing and support spin supercurrent, overcoming the usual conflict between ferromagnetism and superconductivity.
conclusion: This work identifies a new class of materials for spin supercurrent, which could be relevant for spintronics and quantum communication applications requiring low-dissipation spin transport.

title: Dipolar-induced Rabi Dynamics And Trapping Of Chiral Magnons In Antiferromagnets
authors: Shaohua Yuan, Chaowei Sui, Jiyong Kang, Jamal Berakdar, And Chenglong Jia
abstract:
Author(s): Shaohua Yuan, Chaowei Sui, Jiyong Kang, Jamal Berakdar, and Chenglong Jia

Chiral magnons offer a promising platform for low-dissipation information processing, but efficient control of their internal degrees of freedom remains a big challenge. Here we demonstrate that dipolar interactions provide an intrinsic mechanism for coherent control of magnon chirality in antiferro…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220402] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Dipolar interactions enable coherent control of magnon chirality in antiferromagnets, offering a mechanism for low-dissipation information processing.
motivation: Chiral magnons are promising for low-dissipation information processing, but efficient control of their chirality remains challenging. This work aims to demonstrate that dipolar interactions can provide intrinsic coherent control.
method: The authors theoretically study dipolar-induced Rabi dynamics in antiferromagnets, using analytical and numerical methods to model the coupling between magnon modes and the resulting chirality dynamics.
result: They show that dipolar interactions can drive Rabi oscillations between magnon modes of opposite chirality, effectively trapping chiral magnons and enabling coherent control.
conclusion: This work establishes dipolar interactions as a tool for coherent manipulation of magnon chirality, with potential applications in magnon-based information processing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Frequency Shifts Due To Relativistic Effects And Retardation In Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, And Claus Lämmerzahl
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, and Claus Lämmerzahl

Space-based quantum communication naturally involves satellites and ground stations exchanging optical signals at high altitudes and large relative velocities. Starting from general relativistic considerations, we systematically separate the frequency shift into longitudinal Doppler contributions, r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023236] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes relativistic frequency shifts in continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) for space-based systems, separating Doppler and gravitational contributions.
motivation: Space-based quantum communication involves high relative velocities and gravitational potentials, which cause frequency shifts that can degrade CV-QKD performance. Understanding these shifts is crucial for practical implementation.
method: The authors start from general relativistic considerations and systematically separate frequency shifts into longitudinal Doppler, transverse Doppler, and gravitational redshift components. They model the impact on CV-QKD protocols.
result: They quantify how relativistic effects and retardation affect the frequency of optical signals, potentially leading to errors or reduced key rates if not compensated.
conclusion: The work provides a framework to correct for relativistic frequency shifts in space-based CV-QKD, enabling more robust satellite-to-ground quantum communication links.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states (squeezed, trisqueezed, etc.) in trapped-ion systems, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: To develop a general technique for creating complex non-Gaussian states in trapped ions, which are important for quantum sensing and error correction but difficult to produce.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with engineered interactions to generate superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, leveraging control over the ion's motional state.
result: They successfully realize arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states, and verify their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile tool for quantum state engineering in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum sensing and error correction, and could be extended to other platforms.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and optical manipulation. This work aims to overcome these limitations.
method: The authors couple circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, enabling quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control via the auxiliary system.
result: They achieve nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for quantum information processing with these long-lived states.
conclusion: This technique enables new possibilities for quantum computing and simulation with circular Rydberg atoms, and could be extended to other hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems, enabling extrapolation beyond training data.
motivation: Simulating time-periodic quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to learn effective Hamiltonians and long-time dynamics efficiently.
method: Fourier neural operators (FNOs) are employed to map initial states to time-evolved observables in frequency space, capturing temporal correlations and learning the Floquet Hamiltonian from trajectory data.
result: FNOs accurately predict observable dynamics and operator growth for driven quantum systems, including extrapolation to longer times and different driving parameters not seen during training.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that neural operators can serve as efficient surrogates for periodic quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum control and understanding thermalization.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates required to generate pseudorandom unitaries, showing that extensive doping is necessary.
motivation: Understanding the resource cost of generating pseudorandom quantum states and unitaries is crucial for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage experiments. The paper aims to determine the minimal non-Clifford resources needed for pseudorandomness.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including entropy accumulation and concentration of measure, to derive lower bounds on the number of T gates or other non-Clifford gates in doped Clifford circuits that achieve approximate unitary designs.
result: They prove that to achieve a sufficiently close approximation to a unitary 2-design, the number of non-Clifford gates must scale linearly with the number of qubits, i.e., extensive doping is necessary. This matches upper bounds from previous constructions.
conclusion: The results imply that pseudorandom unitaries require a significant overhead of non-Clifford resources, which has implications for the efficiency of quantum algorithms and the security of quantum cryptographic protocols.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates radio-frequency gate reflectometry for fast, noninvasive readout of a minimal Kitaev chain device, resolving charge and parity dynamics relevant for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: To enable fast and noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems, which is crucial for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits and understanding their parity dynamics.
method: The authors use radio-frequency gate reflectometry on a minimal Kitaev chain device, measuring the reflected signal to probe charge and parity states.
result: They successfully resolve key processes and parity dynamics, demonstrating the viability of gate reflectometry for readout in such hybrid superconductor-semiconductor devices.
conclusion: This work provides a readout technique that can accelerate the development of topological qubits and offers insights into the physics of Kitaev chains.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems, unifying diverse approaches across physics subfields.
motivation: Open quantum systems are central to quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate. This Colloquium aims to provide a unified framework to relate different simulation techniques.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework and survey various time-propagation methods, including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: The review categorizes and compares methods for simulating non-Markovian dynamics, showing how they can be understood within a single framework and identifying their respective strengths and limitations.
conclusion: The unified perspective aids in selecting appropriate simulation methods for specific problems and suggests future directions for developing more efficient algorithms, with implications for quantum thermodynamics, quantum information, and many-body physics.

title: Exact Distinguishability Between Real-valued And Complex-valued Haar Random Quantum States
authors: Tristan Nemoz, Romain Alléaume, And Peter Brown
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2120 (2026).

Haar random states are fundamental objects in quantum information theory and quantum computing. We study the density matrix resulting from sampling [MATH] copies of a [MATH]-dimensional quantum state according to the Haar measure on the orthogonal group. In particular, we analytically compute its spectral decomposition. This allows us to compute exactly the trace distance between [MATH]-copies of a real Haar random state and [MATH]-copies of a complex Haar random state. Using this we show a lower-bound on the approximation parameter of real-valued state [MATH]-designs and improve the lower-bound on the number of copies required for imaginarity testing.

.
tldr: The paper analytically computes the spectral decomposition of the density matrix from multiple copies of Haar random states on the orthogonal group, enabling exact trace distance between real and complex Haar random states and improved bounds on real-valued state designs and imaginarity testing.
motivation: Haar random states are fundamental in quantum information, but the distinction between real and complex random states is not fully understood. This work aims to quantify the difference and provide exact results for trace distance.
method: The authors analytically compute the spectral decomposition of the density matrix obtained by sampling multiple copies of a quantum state according to the Haar measure on the orthogonal group, using representation theory and combinatorial techniques.
result: They obtain exact expressions for the trace distance between k copies of a real Haar random state and k copies of a complex Haar random state, and derive a lower bound on the approximation parameter of real-valued state k-designs, improving the lower bound on the number of copies required for imaginarity testing.
conclusion: The results provide a rigorous understanding of the distinguishability of real vs. complex random states, with implications for quantum state designs and the resource theory of imaginarity.

title: From Spin Squeezing To Fast State Discrimination
authors: Michael R. Geller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2108 (2026).

There is great interest in generating and controlling entanglement in Bose-Einstein condensates and similar ensembles for use in quantum computation, simulation, and sensing. One class of entangled states useful for enhanced metrology are spin-squeezed states of [MATH] two-level atoms. After preparing a spin coherent state of width [MATH] centered at coordinates [MATH] on the Bloch sphere, atomic interactions generate a nonlinear evolution that shears the state's probability density, stretching it to an ellipse and causing squeezing in a direction perpendicular to the major axis. Here we consider the same setup but in the [MATH] limit . This shrinks the initial coherent state to zero area. Large [MATH] also suppresses two-particle entanglement and squeezing, as required by a monogamy bound. The torsion (1-axis twist) is still present, however, and the center of the large [MATH] coherent state evolves as a qubit governed by a two-state Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The resulting nonlinearity is known to be a powerful resource in quantum computation. It can be used to implement single-input quantum state discrimination, an impossibility within linear one-particle quantum mechanics. We obtain a solution to the discrimination problem in terms of a Viviani curve on the Bloch sphere. We also consider an open-system variant containing both Bloch sphere torsion and dissipation. In this case it should be possible to generate two basins of attraction within the Bloch ball, having a shared boundary that can be used for a type of autonomous state discrimination. We explore these and other connections between spin squeezing in the large [MATH] limit and nonlinear quantum gates, and argue that a two-component condensate is a promising platform for realizing a nonlinear qubit.

.
tldr: This paper explores the large-N limit of spin squeezing in Bose-Einstein condensates, revealing a nonlinear qubit dynamics that enables quantum state discrimination and autonomous state discrimination in open systems.
motivation: To understand the behavior of spin squeezing in the large-N limit where two-particle entanglement is suppressed, and to exploit the resulting nonlinearity for quantum computation and state discrimination.
method: The authors analyze the evolution of a spin coherent state under one-axis twisting in the large-N limit, deriving a nonlinear Gross-Pitaevskii equation for the qubit dynamics. They also consider an open-system variant with dissipation.
result: In the large-N limit, the center of the coherent state evolves as a nonlinear qubit, enabling single-input quantum state discrimination described by a Viviani curve on the Bloch sphere. The open-system variant can generate two basins of attraction for autonomous state discrimination.
conclusion: Two-component Bose-Einstein condensates are a promising platform for realizing nonlinear qubits with applications in quantum state discrimination and potentially quantum computation.

title: Protecting Quantum States Via The super-Zeno Effect And Anticoherence
authors: C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, And L. Hanotel
abstract:
Author(s): C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, and L. Hanotel

The authors introduce a protocol that combines the quantum super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise arising from spin interactions of polynomial order =1 a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations, while a spin-/2 example achieves average fidelity with short-time scaling −F¯∝
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a protocol combining the super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to protect quantum states from polynomial spin interactions.
motivation: To develop a method for protecting quantum states against noise from spin interactions, which is relevant for quantum information processing.
method: The protocol uses frequent projective measurements (super-Zeno effect) on spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise from polynomial spin operators.
result: For spin-1, a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations; for spin-1/2, average fidelity scales as 1 - F̄ ∝ t^4, showing improved protection.
conclusion: The combination of super-Zeno and anticoherence offers a new way to protect quantum states, with potential applications in quantum sensing and memory.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: This review explores how massive quantum systems can probe gravity, including tests of gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly tested, and to guide experimental searches for quantum gravity effects.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (e.g., gravity-induced decoherence, entanglement mediation) and experimental platforms (e.g., matter-wave interferometry, levitated particles).
result: It summarizes current theoretical proposals and experimental progress, highlighting that gravity can cause decoherence and potentially mediate entanglement between massive particles.
conclusion: Future experiments with massive quantum systems may reveal the quantum nature of gravity, but the paper does not present new results; it is a broad review.

title: Superballistic Flow Of Viscous Electron Fluid Induced By Edge Magnetoplasmons In Point Contacts
authors: Xinghao Wang
Wenfeng Zhang
Loren N. Pfeiffer
Kirk W. Baldwin
K. W. West
Rui-Rui Du
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports superballistic electron flow in point contacts under microwave irradiation, attributed to edge magnetoplasmons.
motivation: To explore hydrodynamic electron transport beyond the ballistic regime and understand the role of edge magnetoplasmons in enhancing conductance.
method: Experimental measurements of conductance in quantum point contacts under microwave irradiation, combined with theoretical modeling of edge magnetoplasmon-induced viscous flow.
result: Observation of conductance exceeding the ballistic limit (superballistic flow) under microwave irradiation, attributed to edge magnetoplasmons driving a viscous electron fluid.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for enhanced electron transport in low-dimensional systems, with potential implications for quantum devices and hydrodynamic electronics.

title: Acoustic Bound Pair States In The Continuum Induced By Off-Site Two-Body Interactions
authors: Zhenhang Pu, Chunbo Hua, Hailong He, Liping Ye, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Manzhu Ke, And Zhengyou Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhang Pu, Chunbo Hua, Hailong He, Liping Ye, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Manzhu Ke, and Zhengyou Liu

A novel many-body bound state in the continuum induced entirely by uniform off-site 2-body interactions is observed by mapping a quantum 1D Bose-Hubbard model onto a 2D macroscopic phononic crystal.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226501] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper observes a novel many-body bound state in the continuum induced by uniform off-site two-body interactions, using a phononic crystal analog of the 1D Bose-Hubbard model.
motivation: To explore many-body bound states in the continuum (BICs) induced by interactions, which are typically studied in single-particle settings, and to demonstrate a classical analog using a macroscopic phononic crystal.
method: The authors map a quantum 1D Bose-Hubbard model with off-site two-body interactions onto a 2D macroscopic phononic crystal, enabling experimental observation of acoustic bound pair states.
result: They observe a novel many-body BIC that arises solely from uniform off-site interactions, not from on-site interactions or lattice engineering.
conclusion: This work provides a classical analog for studying interaction-induced many-body BICs, with potential implications for understanding quantum many-body physics and designing acoustic devices.

title: Evidence Of Chiral Fermion Edge Modes Through Geometric Engineering Of Thermal Hall Effect In $α\text{−}{\mathrm{RuCl}}_{3}$
authors: Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. Mcguire, And Jiaqiang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. McGuire, and Jiaqiang Yan

The experimental observation of half-integer-quantized thermal Hall conductivity in the Kitaev candidate material [MATH] has served as a signature of non-Abelian anyons through an associated chiral Majorana edge mode. However, both the reproducibility of the quantized thermal…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental evidence of chiral fermion edge modes in α-RuCl3 via geometric engineering of the thermal Hall effect, supporting the existence of non-Abelian anyons.
motivation: To confirm the presence of chiral Majorana edge modes in the Kitaev candidate material α-RuCl3, which is a signature of non-Abelian anyons, and to address reproducibility issues in thermal Hall measurements.
method: The authors geometrically engineer the thermal Hall effect by designing specific sample geometries to isolate edge contributions, and measure thermal Hall conductivity at low temperatures.
result: They observe half-integer-quantized thermal Hall conductivity consistent with chiral Majorana edge modes, providing strong evidence for non-Abelian anyons.
conclusion: The findings confirm the existence of chiral edge modes in α-RuCl3, advancing the understanding of topological order and potential applications in topological quantum computing.

title: Hyperentanglement-based Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Quantum machine learning integrates quantum features such as superposition and entanglement into learning processes, offering the potential to outperform classical methods in certain tasks. Among these approaches, quantum reservoir computing (QRC) has attracted considerable attention due to its simp…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062416] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hyperentanglement-based quantum reservoir computing scheme that uses multiple degrees of freedom of photons to enhance computational performance.
motivation: To improve the performance of quantum reservoir computing by leveraging hyperentanglement, which provides more resources for information processing.
method: The authors design a quantum reservoir using hyperentangled photons (e.g., polarization and orbital angular momentum) and analyze its dynamics and computational capabilities.
result: The hyperentanglement-based reservoir shows enhanced memory capacity and nonlinear processing ability compared to conventional entanglement-based reservoirs.
conclusion: Hyperentanglement offers a promising resource for quantum reservoir computing, potentially leading to more powerful quantum machine learning systems.

title: Optimizing Doppler Laser Cooling Protocols For Quantum Sensing With Three-dimensional Ion Crystals In A Penning Trap
authors: John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, And Scott E. Parker
abstract:
Author(s): John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, and Scott E. Parker

Large, three-dimensional (3D) trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity in quantum sensing protocols, and are expected to be implemented as platforms in near-future experiments. However, numerical techniques used to study the laser cooling of such crystals are inefficient as the number of ions…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063103] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes Doppler laser cooling protocols for large 3D ion crystals in Penning traps to enhance quantum sensing, but does not directly address the user's specific interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Large 3D trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity in quantum sensing, but existing numerical techniques for studying laser cooling are inefficient for large ion numbers.
method: The authors develop and optimize Doppler laser cooling protocols using numerical simulations tailored to 3D ion crystals in a Penning trap.
result: Optimized cooling protocols achieve lower temperatures and faster cooling times, enabling better performance for quantum sensing applications.
conclusion: The work provides practical cooling strategies for large ion crystals, but its focus on experimental cooling techniques is tangential to the user's research directions.

title: Slow-light-enhanced Photon Drag In A Tunneling-coupled Quantum-dot System
authors: Muhammad Idrees, Xiaosen Yang, Fazal Badshah, And Zareen A. Khan
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Idrees, Xiaosen Yang, Fazal Badshah, and Zareen A. Khan

We present a theoretical study of enhanced lateral and rotary photon drag within a four-level quantum-dot setup under the effect of dual interdot tunneling. Using the density-matrix formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the susceptibility, group index, and phase index under weak-field cond…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063709] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies slow-light-enhanced photon drag in a tunneling-coupled quantum-dot system, focusing on optical properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore enhanced photon drag effects using slow light in a quantum-dot system with interdot tunneling, which may have applications in optical switching and sensing.
method: Theoretical analysis using density-matrix formalism to derive susceptibility, group index, and phase index under weak-field conditions.
result: Enhanced lateral and rotary photon drag due to slow light and dual interdot tunneling.
conclusion: The findings may enable novel optical devices, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Revealing Emergent Many-body Phenomena By Analyzing Large-scale Space-time Records Of Monitored Quantum Systems
authors: Marcel Cech, Cecilia de Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, And Federico Carollo
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Cech, Cecilia De Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, and Federico Carollo

Midcircuit measurements allow the probing of quantum many-body dynamics with spatial and temporal resolution. In this work, the authors discuss how these records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in space-time.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060201] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows how midcircuit measurement records in monitored quantum systems can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in space-time.
motivation: To demonstrate that space-time records from midcircuit measurements can be used to detect and characterize emergent many-body phenomena, such as quantum phases and transitions.
method: The authors analyze large-scale space-time records obtained from monitored quantum many-body systems, likely using numerical simulations or tensor network methods to extract signatures of emergent behavior.
result: They find that measurement records contain sufficient information to identify emergent many-body phenomena, providing a new tool for probing quantum dynamics.
conclusion: This approach opens avenues for using measurement data to study complex quantum systems, but its direct application to the user's specific interests (thermodynamics, foundations, communication, hybrid systems) is limited.

title: Stabilizer Rényi Entropy For Translation-invariant Matrix Product States
authors: Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Su Yi, And Jian Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Su Yi, and Jian Cui

Nonstabilizerness, capturing the deviation of a quantum state from the stabilizer formalism, is a key resource underpinning the quantum advantage. The recently introduced stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) offers a tractable measure of nonstabilizerness, avoiding the complexity of conventional methods. …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062414] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stabilizer Rényi entropy as a measure of nonstabilizerness in translation-invariant matrix product states.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its computation is often complex. The authors aim to develop efficient methods for translation-invariant matrix product states.
method: The authors use tensor network techniques to compute stabilizer Rényi entropy for translation-invariant matrix product states, leveraging the structure of such states.
result: They derive formulas and demonstrate efficient computation of SRE for certain classes of states, showing scaling behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for quantifying nonstabilizerness in many-body systems, with potential applications in quantum computing and condensed matter.

title: Entanglement-enhanced Correlation Propagation In The One-dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Mathias Mikkelsen And Ippei Danshita
abstract:
Author(s): Mathias Mikkelsen and Ippei Danshita

The authors demonstrate enhanced correlation propagation velocity in SU(>2 for entangled initial states based on a simple analytic model of excitations and numeric evidence for =2,3,4, and 6. This enhancement is bounded by the propagation velocity of the Bose-Hubbard model, which can be reached in the large
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061301] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that entangled initial states enhance correlation propagation velocity in SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models, bounded by the Bose-Hubbard velocity.
motivation: To understand how entanglement affects quantum dynamics and correlation spreading in many-body systems with SU(N) symmetry.
method: Analytic model of excitations and numerical simulations for N=2,3,4,6 using time-dependent methods.
result: Entangled initial states lead to faster correlation propagation compared to product states, with the velocity approaching the Bose-Hubbard limit for large N.
conclusion: The work provides insights into entanglement-enhanced transport, relevant for quantum simulation and information propagation in ultracold atoms.

title: Bosonic Content Of Three-fermion Highest-spin States
authors: Jerzy Cioslowski, Krzysztof Strasburger, And Denis K. Sunko
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2121 (2026).

A rigorous characterization of the information content of any highest-spin three-fermion wave function is presented. It is based upon a formal decomposition of the wave function into a finite set of fixed invariants, called shapes, whose sole purpose is to satisfy the Pauli principle, and a variable part, constituting the bosonic excitations of these invariants, that provides its physical content. As an example, this decomposition is applied to a benchmark-quality approximate wave function of the lowest-energy quartet electronic state of the lithium atom. This wave function, which comprises hundreds of basis functions, is reduced to eleven shape blocks, only five of which are numerically significant. Such a compact characterization is a generic example of the appearance of superselection rules in configuration space, and provides a qualitative aid in the search for robust few-particle entangled states.

.
tldr: The paper decomposes three-fermion highest-spin wave functions into fixed invariants (shapes) and bosonic excitations, applied to lithium's quartet state, revealing compact structure.
motivation: To characterize the information content of three-fermion highest-spin states and understand the role of Pauli principle versus physical excitations.
method: Formal decomposition of wave function into shape invariants and bosonic excitations; applied to a benchmark-quality approximate wave function of lithium's lowest-energy quartet state.
result: The wave function reduces to eleven shape blocks, only five numerically significant, demonstrating a superselection rule in configuration space.
conclusion: Provides compact characterization of entangled few-fermion states, aiding search for robust entangled states, but limited direct relevance to user's interests.

title: Tensor Cross Interpolation Of Purities In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Dmytro Kolisnyk, Raimel A. Medina, Romain Vasseur, And Maksym Serbyn
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2114 (2026).

A defining feature of quantum many-body systems is the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space with the number of degrees of freedom. This exponential complexity naïvely renders a complete state characterization, for instance via the complete set of bipartite Renyi entropies for all disjoint regions, a challenging task. Recently, a compact way of storing subregions' purities by encoding them as amplitudes of a fictitious quantum wave function, known as entanglement feature, was proposed. Notably, the entanglement feature can be a simple object even for highly entangled quantum states. However the complexity and practical usage of the entanglement feature for general quantum states has not been explored. In this work, we demonstrate that the entanglement feature can be efficiently learned using only a polynomial amount of samples in the number of degrees of freedom through the so-called tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm, assuming it is expressible as a finite bond dimension MPS. We benchmark this learning process on Haar and random MPS states, confirming analytic expectations. Applying the TCI algorithm to quantum eigenstates of various one dimensional quantum systems, we identify cases where eigenstates have entanglement feature learnable with TCI. We conclude with possible applications of the learned entanglement feature, such as quantifying the distance between different entanglement patterns and finding the optimal one-dimensional ordering of physical indices in a given state, highlighting the potential utility of the proposed purity interpolation method.

.
tldr: The paper introduces a tensor cross interpolation method to efficiently learn the entanglement feature (purities of all subregions) of quantum many-body states, assuming it can be represented as a matrix product state.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in many-body systems is exponentially hard; the entanglement feature offers a compact representation, but its practical learning for general states was unexplored.
method: The authors apply tensor cross interpolation (TCI) to learn the entanglement feature as a matrix product state, using polynomial samples in the number of degrees of freedom.
result: TCI successfully learns the entanglement feature for Haar random states and random MPS, and for eigenstates of certain 1D quantum systems, enabling tasks like quantifying entanglement pattern distances and finding optimal qubit ordering.
conclusion: The method provides a practical tool for entanglement characterization and may aid in quantum state tomography and optimization of quantum architectures.

title: Phase-Sensitive Measurements On A Fermi–Hubbard Quantum Processor
authors: Alberto R. Cavallar, Luis Escalera-Moreno, Titus Franz, Timon Hilker, J. Ignacio Cirac, Philipp M. Preiss, And Benjamin F. Schiffer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2103 (2026).

Fermionic quantum processors are a promising platform for quantum simulation of correlated fermionic matter. In this work, we study a hardware-efficient protocol for measuring complex expectation values of the time-evolution operator, commonly referred to as Loschmidt echoes, with fermions in an optical superlattice. We analyze the algorithm for the Fermi–Hubbard model at half-filling as well as at finite doping. The method relies on global quench dynamics and short imaginary time evolution, the latter being realized by architecture-tailored pulse sequences starting from a product state of plaquettes. Our numerical results show that complex Loschmidt echoes can be efficiently obtained for large many-body states over a broad spectral range. This allows one to measure spectral properties of the Fermi–Hubbard model, such as the local density of states, and paves the way for the study of finite-temperature properties in current fermionic quantum simulators.

.
tldr: This paper presents a protocol for measuring Loschmidt echoes on a fermionic quantum processor to study spectral properties of the Fermi-Hubbard model.
motivation: To enable measurement of complex expectation values and spectral properties in fermionic quantum simulators, which are crucial for understanding correlated fermionic matter.
method: The protocol uses global quench dynamics and short imaginary time evolution implemented via pulse sequences on an optical superlattice, starting from a product state of plaquettes.
result: Numerical results show that complex Loschmidt echoes can be efficiently obtained for large many-body states over a broad spectral range, allowing measurement of the local density of states.
conclusion: This work paves the way for studying finite-temperature properties in current fermionic quantum simulators, but does not directly address the user's specific interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, or quantum communication.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms

abstract:

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.

motivation: To survey the potential advantages of qudits over qubits in quantum computing, particularly for gate decomposition and algorithm efficiency.

title: On The Dynamical Lie Algebras Of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms
authors: Jonathan Allcock, Miklos Santha, Pei Yuan, And Shengyu Zhang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2119 (2026).

Dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) have emerged as a valuable tool in the study of parameterized quantum circuits, helping to characterize both their expressiveness and trainability. In particular, the absence or presence of barren plateaus (BPs) – flat regions in parameter space that prevent the efficient training of variational quantum algorithms – has recently been shown to be intimately related to quantities derived from the associated DLA. In this work, we investigate DLAs for the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), one of the most studied variational quantum algorithms for solving graph MaxCut and other combinatorial optimization problems. While DLAs for QAOA circuits have been studied before, existing results have either been based on numerical evidence, or else correspond to DLA generators specifically chosen to be universal for quantum computation on a subspace of states. We initiate an analytical study of barren plateaus and other statistics of QAOA algorithms, and give bounds on the dimensions of the corresponding DLAs and their centers for general graphs. We then focus on the [MATH]-vertex cycle and complete graphs. For the cycle graph we give an explicit basis, identify its decomposition into the direct sum of a [MATH]-dimensional center and a semisimple component isomorphic to [MATH] copies of [MATH]. We give an explicit basis for this isomorphism, and a closed-form expression for the variance of the cost function, proving the absence of BPs. For the complete graph we prove that the dimension of the DLA is [MATH] and give an explicit basis for the DLA.

.
tldr: This paper analytically studies dynamical Lie algebras of QAOA circuits for MaxCut on cycle and complete graphs, proving absence of barren plateaus for the cycle graph and giving explicit DLA dimensions and bases.
motivation: To understand the trainability and expressiveness of QAOA, specifically whether barren plateaus occur, by analyzing the underlying dynamical Lie algebras.
method: Analytical derivation of DLA dimensions, centers, and decompositions for general graphs, with explicit calculations for cycle and complete graphs using representation theory and Lie algebra techniques.
result: For cycle graphs, the DLA decomposes into a 2-dimensional center and a semisimple component isomorphic to multiple copies of su(2), leading to a closed-form variance of the cost function and proving no barren plateaus. For complete graphs, the DLA dimension is n^2 - 1 with an explicit basis.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous analytical results on QAOA trainability, showing that certain graph structures avoid barren plateaus, and offers tools for further study of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Bosonic Quantum Computational Complexity
authors: Ulysse Chabaud, Michael Joseph, Saeed Mehraban, And Arsalan Motamedi
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2110 (2026).

Quantum computing involving physical systems with continuous degrees of freedom, such as the quantum states of light, has recently attracted significant interest. However, a well-defined quantum complexity theory for these bosonic computations over infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces is missing. In this work, we lay foundations for such a research program. We introduce natural complexity classes and problems based on bosonic generalizations of BQP, the local Hamiltonian problem, and QMA. We uncover several relationships and subtle differences between standard Boolean classical and discrete variable quantum complexity classes and identify outstanding open problems. In particular: 1. We show that the power of quadratic (Gaussian) quantum dynamics is equivalent to the class BQL. More generally, we define classes of continuous-variable quantum polynomial time computations with a bounded probability of error based on higher-degree gates. Due to the infinite dimensional Hilbert space, it is not a priori clear whether a decidable upper bound can be obtained for these classes. We identify complete problems for these classes and demonstrate a BQP lower and EXPSPACE upper bound. We further show that the problem of computing expectation values of polynomial bosonic observables is in PSPACE. 2. We prove that the problem of deciding the boundedness of the spectrum of a bosonic Hamiltonian is co-NP-hard. Furthermore, we show that the problem of finding the minimum energy of a bosonic Hamiltonian critically depends on the non-Gaussian stellar rank of the family of energy-constrained states one optimizes over: for constant stellar rank, it is NP-complete; for polynomially-bounded rank, it is in QMA; for unbounded rank, it is undecidable.

.
tldr: This paper establishes foundations for bosonic quantum complexity theory, defining continuous-variable complexity classes and analyzing the hardness of bosonic Hamiltonian problems.
motivation: Quantum computing with continuous-variable systems (e.g., light) lacks a well-defined complexity theory, hindering understanding of their computational power and limitations.
method: The authors introduce bosonic generalizations of BQP, QMA, and the local Hamiltonian problem, and analyze their relationships to classical and discrete-variable quantum complexity classes using techniques from computational complexity theory.
result: Gaussian quantum dynamics is equivalent to BQL; higher-degree gate classes have BQP lower and EXPSPACE upper bounds; expectation values of polynomial bosonic observables are in PSPACE; bosonic Hamiltonian problems range from NP-complete to undecidable depending on the stellar rank.
conclusion: The work provides a complexity-theoretic framework for bosonic computations, revealing new classes and open problems, and highlighting the role of non-Gaussian resources in computational hardness.

title: Optimizing Qubo On A Quantum Computer By Mimicking Imaginary Time Evolution
authors: Yahui Chai And Alice Di Tucci
abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum–classical algorithm for solving quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems using an imaginary time evolution-mimicking circuit (ITEMC). The circuit parameters are optimized to mimic short-time ITE, using only single- and two-qubit expectation values. This significantly reduces the measurement overhead by avoiding full energy evaluation. By updating the initial state based on results from last step iteratively, the algorithm quickly converges to the low-energy solutions. With a pre-sorting step that optimizes quantum gate ordering based on QUBO coefficients, the convergence is further improved. Our classical simulations achieve approximation ratios above up to 150 qubits. Furthermore, the linear scaling of entanglement entropy with system size suggests that the circuit is challenging to simulate classically using tensor networks. We also demonstrate hardware runs on IBM’s device for 40, 60, and 80 qubits, and obtain solutions compatible with that from simulated annealing.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for QUBO problems using an imaginary time evolution-mimicking circuit.
motivation: To solve QUBO problems efficiently on near-term quantum devices by reducing measurement overhead and improving convergence.
method: Optimizes circuit parameters to mimic short-time imaginary time evolution using only single- and two-qubit expectation values, with iterative updates and pre-sorting of gates.
result: Achieves approximation ratios above 0.9 for up to 150 qubits in simulation, and demonstrates hardware runs on IBM devices for 40, 60, and 80 qubits.
conclusion: The algorithm shows promise for QUBO on quantum computers, but its relevance to the user's interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, communication, or hybrid systems is indirect.

tldr: This paper studies Kondo physics in quantum wires coupled to a repulsive spin impurity, with potential realizations in ultracold ytterbium atoms.
motivation: To understand how correlations in one-dimensional fermionic environments affect the Kondo effect, particularly with repulsive impurities.
method: Theoretical analysis using renormalization group and numerical methods to study the Kondo model in quantum wires.
result: Identified a pathway to Kondo physics with repulsive impurities and proposed ytterbium atoms as a platform for experimental realization.
conclusion: Provides insights into strongly correlated 1D systems and suggests new experimental directions for Kondo physics.

title: Convolutional Transformer Wave Functions
authors: Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, And Markus Heyl
abstract:

A new study introduces the convolutional transformer wave function, an architecture that, unlike earlier transformer-based approaches, properly harnesses the attention mechanism while respecting the symmetries of quantum systems, setting new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022040] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a convolutional transformer wave function that respects symmetries and sets new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.
motivation: To develop a neural network architecture for quantum many-body systems that properly utilizes attention mechanisms while respecting physical symmetries.
method: Combines convolutional layers with transformer attention in a wave function ansatz, enforcing symmetries via equivariant designs.
result: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on frustrated spin systems and quantum dynamics simulations.
conclusion: The architecture offers a powerful tool for quantum many-body problems, with potential extensions to other physical systems.

A variational method is presented for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems, combining a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022042] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A variational method combining shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to prepare excited states of many-body quantum systems, demonstrated on disordered spin chains with tensor networks.
motivation: To develop a method for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems without explicit matrix inversion, which is computationally expensive.
method: Combines a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution, implemented via tensor-network simulations in a framework compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations.
result: The method successfully prepares excited states of disordered spin chains, as demonstrated in numerical simulations.
conclusion: The approach offers a scalable way to access excited states in many-body systems, with potential applications in quantum chemistry and condensed matter physics, and is amenable to near-term quantum devices.

Lattice gauge theories (LGTs) provide a powerful framework for studying nonperturbative phenomena in gauge theories. However, conventional approaches such as Monte Carlo (MC) simulations in imaginary time are limited, as they do not allow real-time evolution and suffer from a sign problem in many im…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023240] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops algorithmic techniques for gauge fixing and enforcing translation invariance in gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair states (PEPS) for lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Lattice gauge theories are important for nonperturbative physics, but conventional Monte Carlo methods suffer from sign problems and cannot handle real-time evolution. Tensor network methods like PEPS offer an alternative, but gauged fermionic PEPS require careful handling of gauge redundancy and symmetries.
method: The authors propose algorithmic procedures for gauge fixing in Gaussian fermionic PEPS and for imposing translation invariance, likely using tensor network contractions and optimization techniques.
result: The paper presents concrete algorithms to fix the gauge degrees of freedom and enforce translation symmetry, which are essential for efficient simulation of lattice gauge theories with PEPS.
conclusion: These algorithmic advances enable more practical simulations of lattice gauge theories using PEPS, potentially allowing studies of real-time dynamics and avoiding sign problems.

title: Straintronics And Twistronics In Bilayer Graphene

abstract:
