The interplay of twist and strain in bilayer graphene enables the formation of moiré patterns and narrow bands that host correlated and topological phases. While magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene has been widely studied, strain provides an additional and realistic control knob for band engineerin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023225] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay of twist and strain in bilayer graphene to engineer moiré patterns and narrow bands for correlated and topological phases.
motivation: To explore strain as an additional control knob for band engineering in twisted bilayer graphene, beyond the widely studied magic-angle configuration.
method: Theoretical modeling and simulations of bilayer graphene under combined twist and strain, analyzing electronic band structure and moiré patterns.
result: Strain can significantly modify the moiré pattern and narrow band properties, offering new ways to tune correlated and topological phases.
conclusion: Strain provides a realistic and versatile tool for band engineering in bilayer graphene, potentially enabling new quantum phases and device applications.

title: Evolving Disorder In non-Hermitian Lattices
authors: I. Komis, E. T. Kokkinakis, K. G. Makris, And E. N. Economou
abstract:

The impact of disorder on wave transport has been extensively studied in Hermitian systems, where static randomness gives rise to Anderson localization. In non-Hermitian lattices, static disorder can lead to peculiar transport features, including jumpy wave evolution. In contrast, much less is known…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023227] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effects of evolving disorder on wave transport in non-Hermitian lattices, revealing novel transport features distinct from static disorder.
motivation: While static disorder in non-Hermitian systems has been studied, the impact of time-varying (evolving) disorder on wave dynamics remains largely unexplored.
method: The authors theoretically analyze wave propagation in non-Hermitian lattices with disorder that evolves in time, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: Evolving disorder leads to unique transport phenomena, such as enhanced or suppressed localization and non-trivial wave dynamics, not seen in static disorder.
conclusion: The work opens new avenues for controlling wave transport in non-Hermitian systems via dynamic disorder, with potential applications in photonics and acoustics.

title: Spinor Pairing Order Enforced By Berry Phase
authors: Yi Li And Grayson R. Frazier
abstract:

Pairing between Fermi surfaces with unequal Chern-number parity is shown to produce an exotic superconducting state characterized by half-integer monopole harmonics and a spinor-valued order parameter. Consequences include a single Bogoliubov-Weyl node that “violates” the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem, protected gapless surface states, and a fractional Mermin-Ho relation for the superfluid velocity.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022037] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a novel superconducting state with spinor order parameter and half-integer monopole harmonics arising from pairing between Fermi surfaces of unequal Chern-number parity.
motivation: To explore exotic superconducting phases that emerge from topological band structures, specifically pairing between Fermi surfaces with different Chern numbers.
method: Theoretical analysis using Berry phase and monopole harmonic formalism to characterize the order parameter and its topological properties.
result: Discovery of a spinor pairing order with half-integer monopole harmonics, a single Bogoliubov-Weyl node violating the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem, protected gapless surface states, and a fractional Mermin-Ho relation.
conclusion: The work reveals a new class of topological superconductivity with unique properties, opening avenues for studying unconventional pairing mechanisms and topological phenomena.

title: Taxonomy Of Prediction
authors: Alexandra Jurgens And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandra Jurgens and James P. Crutchfield

A prediction makes a claim about a system's future given knowledge of its past. A retrodiction makes a claim about its past given knowledge of its future. The bidirectional machine is an ambidextrous hidden Markov chain that does both optimally by making explicit in its state structure all statistic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023218] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the bidirectional machine, a hidden Markov model that optimally performs both prediction and retrodiction by encoding all statistical dependencies in its state structure.
motivation: To develop a unified framework for optimal prediction and retrodiction in stochastic processes, addressing the asymmetry between forward and backward inference.
method: The authors construct a bidirectional hidden Markov chain that captures both predictive and retrodictive statistics, leveraging computational mechanics and information theory.
result: The bidirectional machine achieves optimal performance for both prediction and retrodiction, revealing the minimal state complexity required for bidirectional inference.
conclusion: This work provides a foundation for understanding temporal inference in complex systems, with potential applications in time series analysis and machine learning.

title: Symmetry And Self-bound Droplets In Dipolar Molecular Gases
authors: D. Baillie
abstract:

tldr: This paper reveals a symmetry structure in dipolar interactions of molecular gases that leads to degeneracies among interaction parameters, enabling control of self-bound droplets.
motivation: To understand and exploit the symmetry of dipolar interactions in degenerate molecular gases dressed by elliptically polarized microwaves, which allows new control of dipolar interactions via engineered anisotropy.
method: Theoretical analysis of the dipolar interaction symmetry and its consequences for interaction parameters, likely using mean-field or beyond-mean-field approaches.
result: Discovery of a symmetry structure that generates degeneracies among interaction parameters, which can be used to tune interactions and stabilize self-bound droplets.
conclusion: The findings provide a new way to control dipolar interactions in molecular gases, with implications for quantum simulation and many-body physics.

result: The paper demonstrates that organic open-shell molecules can host strongly correlated phenomena, influencing transport properties.
conclusion: The findings suggest that organic molecules are viable platforms for studying strongly correlated physics, with potential implications for molecular electronics and quantum materials.

result: Changing average densities alters the composition of coexisting phases and can lead to various pattern formations, including traveling waves and static patterns.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling phase behavior in active mixtures, with potential applications in synthetic active matter.

method: The authors develop a complete stochastic calculus for Markov-jump processes, extending Itô calculus to include jump contributions and deriving a unified description in the continuum limit.
result: A unified stochastic calculus is established that encompasses both diffusion and jump dynamics, enabling consistent treatment of pathwise observables across different process types.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational mathematical tool for studying stochastic processes with jumps, with potential applications in nonequilibrium statistical mechanics and beyond.

method: Conceptual analysis and perspective, drawing on known biophysical principles of phase separation and information theory.
result: Suggests that condensates can act as computational elements, processing multiple inputs simultaneously through phase behavior.
conclusion: Phase transitions may offer a novel mechanism for cellular computation, with implications for synthetic biology and understanding biological information processing.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models

motivation: To challenge the traditional assumption that macroscopic properties are independent of system shape in the thermodynamic limit, by studying quantum dimer models.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of quantum dimer models on lattices with different domain shapes, examining ground state properties and phase separation.
result: Domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, leading to quantum phase separation that violates the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The findings suggest that in certain quantum systems, the thermodynamic limit may not hold, with implications for understanding quantum phases and phase transitions.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič

method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing time and thermalization time in quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite in many-body chaotic systems, and the Trotterization transition is generically a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the limitations of Trotterization and provide a method to compute thermalization time, with implications for quantum simulation.

conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum algorithms for learning hidden structures, with potential applications in quantum error correction and complexity theory.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, focusing on confinement in lattice gauge theories.
motivation: To understand the real-time dynamics of string breaking in confining gauge theories, which is relevant for quantum simulation of high-energy physics.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion quantum simulator to emulate a spin chain with long-range interactions that mimic confinement, and compare adiabatic and diabatic protocols.
result: They observe distinct string-breaking dynamics, including regimes where strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum behavior, and identify experimentally accessible signatures.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into non-equilibrium dynamics of confinement and demonstrates the power of quantum simulators for studying gauge theories.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: To enable scalable classical simulation of logical magic state preparation, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing but typically computationally expensive.
method: The authors develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the final measurement, reducing the simulation complexity for a large class of protocols.
result: The method makes classical simulation of logical magic state preparation scalable and efficient, as demonstrated on relevant examples.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing magic state preparation, with implications for resource estimation and verification in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new family of quantum LDPC codes that achieve single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: To improve fault-tolerant quantum error correction by reducing the overhead of syndrome extraction and enabling single-shot error correction.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes that are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their performance via numerical simulations.
result: The proposed codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths compared to existing codes.
conclusion: These codes offer a promising path toward practical fault-tolerant quantum computing with reduced resource requirements.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and realistic experimental tools.
motivation: To develop a general and efficient protocol for preparing multimode multi-photon quantum states, which are important for quantum information processing.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose target photonic states into a sequence of operations achievable with current experimental setups.
result: They show that any photonic state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic tools.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic framework for photonic state preparation, potentially advancing quantum computing and communication experiments.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant quantum computation of molecular energies using error-corrected logical qubits on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated into practical quantum chemistry simulations, improving accuracy despite hardware noise.
method: The authors use noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets to implement a partially fault-tolerant algorithm for computing molecular energies on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They achieve a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies, demonstrating improved accuracy over non-error-corrected approaches.
conclusion: This work advances the feasibility of reliable quantum simulations for chemistry, but full fault-tolerance remains a future goal.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.
motivation: To develop a quantum algorithm that can efficiently analyze eigenvalue spectra, particularly identifying multiplicities, which is important for many applications but classically hard.
method: The paper proposes a quantum filtering algorithm that uses quantum signal processing or related techniques to filter out eigenvalues and estimate their multiplicities.
result: The algorithm can identify clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities with improved efficiency compared to classical methods, going beyond worst-case complexity bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for spectral analysis on quantum computers, with potential applications in quantum chemistry, condensed matter physics, and other fields requiring eigenvalue decomposition.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops fault-tolerant protocols for Majorana-based quantum codes, focusing on gates, measurements, and high-rate code constructions.
motivation: To extend fault-tolerant quantum computing techniques from qubit-based systems to fermionic systems, specifically Majorana-based codes, which are promising for topological quantum computation.
method: Generalization of qubit error correction and fault-tolerant protocols to fermionic processes, including design of gates, measurements, and code constructions.
result: Creation of fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes, enabling gates, measurements, and high-rate codes.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana-based codes, with implications for topological quantum computing.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits easier to simulate classically via Pauli propagation.
motivation: To understand the impact of noise on classical simulability of quantum circuits and to develop efficient simulation methods.
method: The authors use Pauli propagation techniques to simulate quantum circuits under arbitrary local noise.
result: Arbitrary local noise reduces the complexity of simulating typical quantum circuits on classical computers.
conclusion: Noisy quantum circuits may be classically tractable, which has implications for quantum advantage experiments.

title: High-Threshold, Low-Overhead And Single-Shot Decodable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory
authors: Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, And Joschka Roffe
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, and Joschka Roffe

Radial codes, a new class of low-density parity-check codes with strong error correction capabilities, tunable parameters, and small size, are shown to be a promising candidate for near-term quantum devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020310] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Radial codes are introduced as a new class of low-density parity-check codes offering high threshold, low overhead, and single-shot decodable fault-tolerant quantum memory.
motivation: To develop quantum error-correcting codes that are practical for near-term devices by achieving high error thresholds, low resource overhead, and single-shot decoding.
method: The authors propose radial codes, a family of LDPC codes with tunable parameters, and analyze their performance using numerical simulations and theoretical bounds.
result: Radial codes demonstrate high error thresholds, low overhead, and single-shot decodability, making them promising for fault-tolerant quantum memory.
conclusion: Radial codes are a strong candidate for near-term quantum devices, but further work is needed to integrate them into full fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks Are Effectively Classically Simulable
authors: Pablo Bermejo, Paolo Braccia, Manuel S. Rudolph, Zoë Holmes, Lukasz Cincio, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Bermejo, Paolo Braccia, Manuel S. Rudolph, Zoë Holmes, Lukasz Cincio, and M. Cerezo

The action of a quantum convolutional neural network, which is a promising architecture for quantum machine learning, can be efficiently simulated by a classical computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020304] Published Mon Apr 06, 2026.
tldr: Quantum convolutional neural networks can be efficiently simulated classically, challenging their quantum advantage.
motivation: To determine whether quantum convolutional neural networks offer a computational advantage over classical methods.
method: The authors analyze the structure of QCNNs and show that their action can be simulated efficiently on a classical computer using tensor network methods.
result: QCNNs are effectively classically simulable, meaning they do not provide exponential speedup for the tasks considered.
conclusion: The findings suggest that QCNNs may not be a viable candidate for near-term quantum advantage, and alternative quantum machine learning architectures should be explored.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism since its experimental realization in 2016.
method: Review article summarizing experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and magneto-optical phenomena.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving, expanding theoretical understanding and opening new directions for applications.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive and unified perspective on how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles, a topic with long history and broad applications.
method: The authors review theoretical frameworks and experimental demonstrations, drawing parallels between optical and acoustic wave phenomena.
result: They show that local densities of energy, momentum, and spin determine forces and torques, enabling applications like optical trapping, acoustic sorting, and pulling forces.
conclusion: The unified approach aids in designing advanced particle manipulation techniques across optics and acoustics.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics using brickwork quantum circuits, focusing on exactly solvable models.
motivation: To provide a pedagogical overview of how space-time duality and brickwork circuits enable exact solutions for quantum many-body dynamics.
method: Review of theoretical framework combining space-time duality with brickwork quantum circuits, drawing analogies with quantum computation.
result: Unified view of dynamical evolution in many-body systems via exactly solvable models based on dual-unitary circuits.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful tool for understanding quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum simulation and computation.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: This review covers exotic electronic states in kagome metals, focusing on topological flat bands, Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena observed in kagome metals, driven by frustrated geometry and strong correlations.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic structure, many-body effects, and emergent phases.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and electronic nematicity, arising from topological flat bands and sublattice interference.
conclusion: The review elucidates key mechanisms and suggests future directions for exploring correlated topological phases in kagome materials.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: This pedagogical review applies field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems using field-theoretic methods, which are powerful but often scattered across different disciplines.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, including path integrals and quantum field theory techniques, to stochastic reaction-diffusion equations.
result: They demonstrate how these methods unify various approaches and can be applied to a wide range of complex systems beyond chemistry.
conclusion: The review highlights the versatility of field-theoretic methods and suggests they can be extended to other areas such as ecology and epidemiology.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with emphasis on synergy across these approaches.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research, highlighting progress and the interplay between experimental, theoretical, and computational methods.
method: Review article synthesizing experimental results, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: The review tracks the evolution of the field, emphasizing the importance of combining experiment, theory, and simulation to understand spin-glass dynamics.
conclusion: The paper identifies future research opportunities in spin glasses, which have broad applications to other physical systems.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: This review covers theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of Kitaev spin liquids, a topic of intense interest in condensed matter physics, and to highlight recent developments in materials and theory.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental results on candidate materials, discussing topological properties like chiral edge modes.
result: Key findings include the identification of leading candidate materials for Kitaev spin liquids and the broad topological properties that characterize them.
conclusion: The review offers essential insights for researchers in quantum spin liquids, but does not directly address the user's specific interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, communication, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze large-scale neural recordings, but does not address quantum systems or information thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how coordinated neural activity in the brain can be described using principles from statistical physics.
method: Review of recent experiments recording electrical activity from thousands of neurons, analyzed with maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques.
result: Statistical physics models can quantitatively reproduce neural activity patterns and reveal reproducible behaviors.
conclusion: Abstract theoretical principles from physics can achieve predictive power in neuroscience, similar to other areas of physics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: This review covers theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions relevant to photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of theoretical approaches to internal conversion, a key photophysical process, and to guide future research in applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper is a review that surveys various theoretical models and methods used to describe internal conversion, including quantum dynamics and nonadiabatic coupling.
result: The review summarizes the state of the art in modeling internal conversion, highlighting different theoretical frameworks and their applicability.
conclusion: The authors suggest that these models can be integrated into studies of photonic and energy harvesting applications, but the paper does not present new findings or direct connections to the user's specific interests.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, particularly Mott insulators, for potential material manipulation and discovery of metastable phases.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving pathways.
result: Key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable orders (superconducting, magnetic, orbital, excitonic) are highlighted.
conclusion: Provides a framework for future research in nonequilibrium strongly correlated systems, with implications for ultrafast control of materials.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their formation interactions and intrinsic quantum features.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of quantum properties of magnetic skyrmions, which have been studied mainly classically, and to highlight their potential for quantum technologies.
method: Review article summarizing theoretical and experimental work on quantum skyrmions, including quantum interactions underlying skyrmion formation and quantum features like superposition and entanglement.
result: Discusses quantum aspects such as skyrmion quantization, quantum dynamics, and possible applications in quantum information processing.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may enable new functionalities in spintronics and quantum computing, but many open questions remain regarding their experimental realization and control.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To provide a systematic overview of the current status and future prospects in the search for spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model, which could reveal new physics and explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper is a review that summarizes theoretical frameworks (e.g., effective field theories) and experimental techniques (e.g., atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and astrophysical observations) used to probe spin-dependent exotic interactions.
result: The review catalogs various exotic boson mediators (e.g., axions, Z' bosons) and their predicted spin-dependent forces, and surveys experimental constraints from a wide range of experiments, highlighting the most stringent limits.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, with many experimental efforts ongoing; future improvements in sensitivity could probe theoretically motivated parameter space.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on physical properties, explaining how violations arise from measurement conditions that break underlying assumptions.
motivation: To clarify apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds in materials and to guide the design of materials with extreme properties.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical results across various fields, identifying which assumptions of classical bounds are violated.
result: Many reported exceedances of bounds are due to non-equilibrium conditions, inhomogeneities, or other assumption violations, not true violations of thermodynamics.
conclusion: Understanding these violations enables the engineering of materials with properties beyond conventional limits, with implications for metamaterials and composites.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data up to the end of 2022.
motivation: To provide an updated, self-consistent set of fundamental constants for use in science and technology.
method: Least-squares adjustment of experimental and theoretical data from various sources.
result: New recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors.
conclusion: The updated constants are essential for precision measurements and theoretical calculations across physics and chemistry.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the current capability to predict coherence times of electron spin qubits using ab initio methods, which is crucial for quantum technologies.
method: Review of cluster expansion techniques and other computational approaches for modeling spin-spin relaxation, with discussion of challenges in higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
result: Cluster expansion methods have matured to reliably predict spin-spin relaxation times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for cases with higher-order perturbations and decoherence from surfaces/interfaces.
conclusion: The field is advancing toward predictive modeling of decoherence, but further development is needed to handle complex environments and higher-order effects.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical progress in realizing quantum many-body systems on fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions using atomic, photonic, and electronic platforms.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries that are difficult to realize naturally, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: The paper surveys multiple experimental platforms (ultracold atoms, photonic systems, electronic circuits) and theoretical approaches for implementing fractal, curved, and higher-dimensional synthetic quantum matter.
result: It highlights key achievements such as the observation of topological states on fractal lattices, simulation of curved space effects, and realization of synthetic dimensions, and discusses open challenges.
conclusion: The field is rapidly advancing, with potential to uncover new physics and enable quantum simulations of exotic spacetimes, but many technical hurdles remain for scaling and control.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: This paper classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras of one-dimensional spin systems with finite Abelian group symmetry using topological invariants.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that preserve a given symmetry, which is important for understanding topological phases and dualities.
method: The authors define subalgebra quantum cellular automata (QCA) on the symmetric subalgebra of a finite Abelian group symmetry, and classify them using two invariants: a homomorphism to anyon permutations in the corresponding gauge theory, and a generalized GNVW index.
result: They show that two subalgebra QCAs are equivalent up to finite-depth symmetric circuits iff they have the same anyon permutation and index. They also show that the Kramers-Wannier duality corresponds to a nontrivial anyon permutation and has an irrational index, preventing extension to a full QCA.
conclusion: The classification provides a complete understanding of symmetric QCAs in one dimension, with implications for dualities and topological phases, but the paper is primarily theoretical and not directly applicable to the user's research interests.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity gains from spin-squeezed states in lossy multi-path atom interferometers, focusing on Bragg diffraction and realistic losses.
motivation: To understand whether spin-squeezed states can improve phase sensitivity in atom interferometers under realistic, non-unitary conditions including losses.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is introduced to model non-unitary interferometers with losses from velocity selectivity and scattering, applied to evaluate one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing can yield several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite losses, but finite temperature reduces the benefits of entanglement.
conclusion: The results suggest ways to optimize interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, advancing precision metrology with atom interferometers.

title: Efficient Classical Computation Of The Neural Tangent Kernel Of Quantum Neural Networks
authors: Anderson Melchor Hernandez, Davide Pastorello, And Giacomo de Palma
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2118 (2026).

We propose an efficient classical algorithm to estimate the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) associated with a broad class of quantum neural networks. These networks consist of arbitrary unitary operators belonging to the Clifford group interleaved with parametric gates given by the time evolution generated by an arbitrary Hamiltonian belonging to the Pauli group. The proposed algorithm leverages a key insight: the average over the distribution of initialization parameters in the NTK definition can be exactly replaced by an average over just four discrete values, chosen such that the corresponding parametric gates are Clifford operations. This reduction enables an efficient classical simulation of the circuit. Combined with recent results establishing the equivalence between wide quantum neural networks and Gaussian processes [Girardi et al., Comm. Math. Phys. 406, 92 (2025); Melchor Hernandez et al., Ann. Henri Poincaré (2025)], our method enables efficient computation of the expected output of wide, trained quantum neural networks, and therefore shows that such networks cannot achieve quantum advantage.

.
tldr: The paper shows that the neural tangent kernel of certain quantum neural networks can be efficiently computed classically, implying no quantum advantage for wide trained QNNs.
motivation: To determine whether quantum neural networks can provide a computational advantage over classical methods, specifically by analyzing the neural tangent kernel.
method: The authors replace the average over initialization parameters in the NTK definition with an average over four discrete Clifford operations, enabling efficient classical simulation.
result: The NTK for a broad class of QNNs can be computed classically in polynomial time, and combined with Gaussian process equivalence, the expected output of wide trained QNNs is classically tractable.
conclusion: Wide quantum neural networks of the considered type cannot achieve quantum advantage, and the work provides a classical algorithm for their analysis.

title: Hidden Time-nonlocal Floquet Symmetries
authors: Sigmund Kohler And Jesús Casado-Pascual
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2112 (2026).

We investigate the Floquet spectrum of a detuned, driven two-level system and show that it exhibits exact quasienergy crossings when the detuning is an integer multiple of the energy quantum of the driving field. This behavior can be explained by a hidden time-nonlocal parity, which allows the Floquet modes to be classified as even or odd. Then a generic feature is the emergence of exact crossings between quasienergies of different parity. A constructive proof of the existence of the symmetry is based on a scalar recurrence relation. Moreover, we present a general scheme for its numerical computation, which can be applied to models beyond the two-level system. Analytical results are illustrated with numerical data.

.
tldr: The paper discovers hidden time-nonlocal Floquet symmetries in driven two-level systems that explain exact quasienergy crossings.
motivation: To understand the origin of exact quasienergy crossings in periodically driven quantum systems, which are not explained by standard symmetries.
method: Analytical derivation using a scalar recurrence relation and numerical computation of the hidden symmetry.
result: Exact quasienergy crossings occur when detuning equals an integer multiple of the driving frequency, classified by a hidden time-nonlocal parity symmetry.
conclusion: The symmetry provides a general framework for analyzing Floquet spectra beyond two-level systems, with potential applications in quantum control.

title: Fully Optimised Variational Simulation Of A Dynamical Quantum Phase Transition On A Trapped-ion Quantum Computer
authors: Lesley Gover, Vinul Wimalaweera, Fariha Azad, Matthew Decross, Michael Foss-Feig, And Andrew G. Green
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2109 (2026).

We time-evolve a translationally invariant quantum state on the Quantinuum H1-1 trapped-ion quantum processor, studying the dynamical quantum phase transition of the transverse field Ising model. This physics requires a delicate cancellation of phases in the many-body wavefunction and presents a tough challenge for current quantum devices. We follow the dynamics using a quantum circuit matrix product state ansatz, optimised for the time-evolution using a fidelity cost function. Sampling costs are mitigated by using the measured values of this circuit as stochastic corrections to a simple classical extrapolation of the ansatz parameters. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of variational quantum time-evolution and reveal a hitherto hidden simplicity of the evolution of the transverse-field Ising model through the dynamical quantum phase transition.

.
tldr: This paper uses a variational quantum circuit matrix product state ansatz on a trapped-ion quantum processor to simulate a dynamical quantum phase transition in the transverse field Ising model.
motivation: To demonstrate the feasibility of variational quantum time-evolution on current quantum hardware for studying dynamical quantum phase transitions, which require delicate phase cancellations.
method: A quantum circuit matrix product state ansatz is optimized for time-evolution using a fidelity cost function, with sampling costs mitigated by using measured circuit values as stochastic corrections to a classical extrapolation of ansatz parameters.
result: The variational approach successfully followed the dynamics of the transverse field Ising model through the dynamical quantum phase transition, revealing a hidden simplicity in the evolution.
conclusion: The results demonstrate the feasibility of variational quantum time-evolution on near-term quantum devices and provide insights into the dynamics of quantum phase transitions.

title: Operator Space Fragmentation In Perturbed Floquet-Clifford Circuits
authors: Marcell D. Kovács, Christopher J. Turner, Lluis Masanes, And Arijeet Pal
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2107 (2026).

Floquet quantum circuits are able to realise a wide range of non-equilibrium quantum states, exhibiting quantum chaos, topological order and localisation. In this work, we investigate the stability of operator localisation and emergence of chaos in random Floquet-Clifford circuits subjected to unitary perturbations which drive them away from the Clifford limit. We construct a nearest-neighbour Clifford circuit with a brickwork pattern and study the effect of including disordered non-Clifford gates. The perturbations are uniformly sampled from single-qubit unitaries with probability [MATH] on each qubit. We show that the interacting model exhibits strong localisation of operators for [MATH] that is characterised by the fragmentation of operator space into disjoint sectors due to the appearance of wall configurations. Such walls give rise to emergent local integrals of motion for the circuit that we construct exactly. We analytically establish the stability of localisation against generic perturbations and calculate the average length of operator spreading tunable by [MATH]. Although our circuit is not separable across any bi-partition, we further show that the operator localisation leads to an entanglement bottleneck, where initially unentangled states remain weakly entangled across typical fragment boundaries. Finally, we study the spectral form factor (SFF) to characterise the chaotic properties of the operator fragments and spectral fluctuations as a probe of non-ergodicity. In the [MATH] model, the emergence of a fragmentation time scale is found before random matrix theory sets in after which the SFF can be approximated by that of the circular unitary ensemble. Our work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity which can be realised on current NISQ devices.

.
tldr: This paper studies operator space fragmentation and localization in perturbed Floquet-Clifford circuits, revealing emergent integrals of motion and entanglement bottlenecks.
motivation: To understand the stability of operator localization and the emergence of chaos in quantum circuits when perturbed away from the Clifford limit.
method: They construct a nearest-neighbour Clifford circuit with a brickwork pattern and add disordered non-Clifford gates, then analyze operator spreading, fragmentation, and spectral form factor.
result: They find strong operator localization for small perturbation probability, characterized by fragmentation into disjoint sectors with wall configurations, and show that this leads to an entanglement bottleneck.
conclusion: The work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity, with potential realization on NISQ devices.

title: Polynomial Time Constructive Decision Algorithm For Multivariable Quantum Signal Processing
authors: Yuki Ito, Hitomi Mori, Kazuki Sakamoto, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2102 (2026).

Quantum signal processing (QSP) and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) have provided a unified framework for understanding many quantum algorithms, including factorization, matrix inversion, and Hamiltonian simulation. As a multivariable version of QSP, multivariable quantum signal processing (M-QSP) is proposed. M-QSP interleaves signal operators corresponding to each variable with signal processing operators, which provides an efficient means to perform multivariable polynomial transformations. However, the necessary and sufficient condition for what types of polynomials can be constructed by M-QSP is unknown. In this paper, we propose a classical algorithm to determine whether a given pair of multivariable Laurent polynomials can be implemented by M-QSP, which returns True or False. As one of the most important properties of this algorithm, its returning True is the necessary and sufficient condition. The proposed classical algorithm runs in polynomial time in the number of variables and signal operators. Our algorithm also provides a constructive method to select the necessary parameters for implementing M-QSP. These findings offer valuable insights for identifying practical applications of M-QSP.

.
tldr: This paper presents a polynomial-time classical algorithm to decide whether a given pair of multivariable Laurent polynomials can be implemented by multivariable quantum signal processing (M-QSP), and provides a constructive method for parameter selection.
motivation: The necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial implementability in M-QSP was unknown, limiting its practical applications.
method: The authors propose a classical algorithm that checks the condition and runs in polynomial time in the number of variables and signal operators.
result: The algorithm returns True if and only if the polynomial pair is implementable, and it also constructs the required parameters.
conclusion: This work provides a constructive decision procedure for M-QSP, enabling identification of practical applications and further algorithmic development.

title: Construction And Decoding Of Quantum Margulis Codes
authors: Michele Pacenti, Dimitris Chytas, And Bane Vasić
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2101 (2026).

Quantum low-density parity-check codes are a promising approach to fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering potential advantages in rate and decoding efficiency. In this work, we introduce quantum Margulis codes, a new class of QLDPC codes derived from Margulis' classical LDPC construction via the two-block group algebra framework. We show that quantum Margulis codes, unlike bivariate bicycle codes which require ordered statistics decoding for effective error correction, can be efficiently decoded using a standard min-sum decoder with linear complexity, when decoded under the code capacity noise model. This is attributed to their Tanner graph structure, which does not exhibit group symmetry, thereby mitigating the well-known problem of error degeneracy in QLDPC decoding. To further enhance performance, we propose an algorithm for constructing 2BGA codes with controlled girth, ensuring a minimum girth of 6 or 8, and use it to generate several quantum Margulis codes of length 240 and 642. We validate our approach through numerical simulations, demonstrating that quantum Margulis codes behave significantly better than BB codes in the error floor region, under min-sum decoding.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum Margulis codes, a new class of QLDPC codes with efficient min-sum decoding and improved error floor performance compared to bivariate bicycle codes.
motivation: To construct QLDPC codes that can be decoded efficiently without ordered statistics decoding, addressing error degeneracy issues in quantum LDPC decoding.
method: Using the two-block group algebra framework to derive quantum Margulis codes from classical Margulis LDPC codes, and proposing an algorithm to control girth (minimum 6 or 8) for code construction.
result: Quantum Margulis codes of lengths 240 and 642 show significantly better error floor performance than bivariate bicycle codes under min-sum decoding with linear complexity.
conclusion: Quantum Margulis codes offer a promising alternative for fault-tolerant quantum computation with efficient decoding, though the work is limited to code capacity noise models and further study under realistic noise is needed.

title: Learning Symmetry-protected Topological Order From Trapped-ion Experiments
authors: Nicolas Sadoune, Ivan Pogorelov, Claire L. Edmunds, Giuliano Giudici, Giacomo Giudice, Christian D. Marciniak, Martin Ringbauer, Thomas Monz, And Lode Pollet
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2100 (2026).

Classical machine learning has proven remarkably useful in post-processing quantum data, yet typical learning algorithms often require prior training to be effective. In this work, we employ a tensorial kernel support vector machine (TK-SVM) to analyze experimental data produced by trapped-ion quantum computers. This unsupervised method benefits from directly interpretable training parameters, allowing it to identify the non-trivial string-order characterizing symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. We apply our technique to two examples: a spin-1/2 model and a spin-1 model, featuring the cluster state and the AKLT state as paradigmatic instances of SPT order, respectively. Using matrix product states, we generate a family of quantum circuits that host a trivial phase and an SPT phase, with a sharp phase transition between them. For the spin-1 case, we implement these circuits on two distinct trapped-ion machines based on qubits and qutrits. Our results demonstrate that the TK-SVM method successfully distinguishes the two phases across all noisy experimental datasets, highlighting its robustness and effectiveness in quantum data interpretation.

.
tldr: This paper uses a tensorial kernel support vector machine to identify symmetry-protected topological order from trapped-ion quantum computer data.
motivation: To demonstrate that unsupervised machine learning can directly interpret experimental quantum data and detect topological phases without prior training.
method: A tensorial kernel support vector machine (TK-SVM) is applied to measurement data from trapped-ion quantum computers, using matrix product states to generate circuits hosting trivial and SPT phases.
result: The TK-SVM successfully distinguishes trivial and SPT phases in both spin-1/2 and spin-1 models, even in noisy experimental data from qubit and qutrit trapped-ion machines.
conclusion: The method is robust and effective for quantum data interpretation, offering a new tool for detecting topological order in near-term quantum devices.

title: Efficient Implementation Of Single Particle Hamiltonians In Exponentially Reduced Qubit Space
authors: Martin Plesch, Martin Friák, And Ijaz Ahamed Mohammad
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2099 (2026).

Current and near-term quantum hardware is constrained by limited qubit counts, circuit depth, and the high cost of repeated measurements. We address these challenges for solid-state Hamiltonians by introducing a logarithmic-qubit encoding that maps a system with [MATH] physical sites onto only [MATH] qubits while maintaining a clear correspondence with the underlying physical model. Within this reduced register, we construct a compatible variational circuit and a Gray-code-inspired measurement strategy whose number of global settings grows only logarithmically with system size. To quantify the overall hardware load, we introduce a volumetric efficiency metric that combines the number of qubits, circuit depth, and the number of measurement settings into a single measure, expressing the overall computation costs. Using this metric, we show that the total space--time sampling volume required in a variational loop can be reduced dramatically from [MATH] to [MATH] for a hardware-efficient ansatz, allowing an exponential reduction in time and size of the quantum hardware. These results demonstrate that large, structured solid-state Hamiltonians can be simulated on substantially smaller quantum registers with controlled sampling overhead and manageable circuit complexity, extending the reach of variational quantum algorithms on near-term devices.

.
tldr: The paper introduces a logarithmic-qubit encoding for simulating single-particle solid-state Hamiltonians on near-term quantum devices, drastically reducing qubit count and measurement settings.
motivation: Current quantum hardware has limited qubit counts and circuit depth, making simulation of large solid-state Hamiltonians challenging. The authors aim to reduce the required quantum resources.
method: They propose a logarithmic-qubit encoding that maps N physical sites to log N qubits, a compatible variational circuit, and a Gray-code-inspired measurement strategy that requires only O(log N) measurement settings.
result: The total space-time sampling volume in a variational loop is reduced from O(N^2) to O(log^2 N), enabling exponential reduction in hardware requirements.
conclusion: The approach allows simulation of large structured Hamiltonians on smaller quantum registers, extending the reach of variational quantum algorithms on near-term devices.

title: The Complexity Of Local Stoquastic Hamiltonians On 2d Lattices
authors: Gabriel Waite And Michael J. Bremner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2097 (2026).

We show the 2-Local Stoquastic Hamiltonian problem on a 2D square qubit lattice is StoqMA-complete. We achieve this by extending the spatially sparse circuit construction of Oliveira and Terhal, as well as the perturbative gadgets of Bravyi, DiVincenzo, Oliveira, and Terhal. Our main contributions demonstrate StoqMA circuits can be made spatially sparse and that geometrical, stoquastic-preserving, perturbative gadgets can be constructed, without an increase to particle dimension.

.
tldr: This paper proves that the 2-Local Stoquastic Hamiltonian problem on a 2D square lattice is StoqMA-complete using spatially sparse circuits and perturbative gadgets.
motivation: To understand the computational complexity of stoquastic Hamiltonians, which are relevant to quantum Monte Carlo methods and adiabatic quantum computing.
method: Extends the spatially sparse circuit construction of Oliveira and Terhal and the perturbative gadgets of Bravyi et al. to show StoqMA-completeness without increasing particle dimension.
result: The 2-Local Stoquastic Hamiltonian problem on a 2D square qubit lattice is StoqMA-complete.
conclusion: This establishes a fundamental complexity result for stoquastic Hamiltonians, with implications for quantum simulation and complexity theory.

title: Quantum Optimal Control For Coherent Spin Dynamics Of Radical Pairs Via Pontryagin Maximum Principle
authors: Ugur G. Abdulla, Jose H. Rodrigues, And Jean-Jacques Slotine
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2096 (2026).

This paper aims to devise the shape of the external electromagnetic field that drives the spin dynamics of radical pairs to a quantum coherent state through maximization of the triplet-born singlet yield in biochemical reactions. The model is a Schrödinger system with spin Hamiltonians given by the sum of Zeeman interaction and hyperfine coupling interaction terms. We introduce a one-parameter family of optimal control problems by coupling the Schrödinger system to a control field through filtering equations for the electromagnetic field. Fréchet differentiability and the Pontryagin Maximum Principle in Hilbert space are proved, and the bang-bang structure of the optimal control is established. A new iterative Pontryagin Maximum Principle (IPMP) method for the identification of the bang-bang optimal control is developed. Numerical simulations based on IPMP and the gradient projection method (GPM) in Hilbert spaces are pursued, and the convergence, stability, and the regularization effect are demonstrated. Comparative analysis of filtering with regular optimal electromagnetic field versus non-filtering with bang-bang optimal field ([MATH][MATH]) demonstrates that the change of the maxima of the singlet yield is less than 1%. The results open a venue for a potential experimental work on magnetoreception as a manifestation of quantum biological phenomena.

.
tldr: This paper uses optimal control theory to maximize singlet yield in radical pair spin dynamics, with potential applications to magnetoreception.
motivation: To understand how external electromagnetic fields can control quantum coherence in radical pairs, which is relevant to biochemical magnetoreception.
method: Formulates an optimal control problem for the Schrödinger equation with Zeeman and hyperfine interactions, proves Fréchet differentiability and Pontryagin Maximum Principle, and develops an iterative PMP algorithm for bang-bang control.
result: The optimal control is bang-bang; numerical simulations show that filtering with regular fields yields less than 1% change in singlet yield compared to bang-bang control.
conclusion: The method provides a framework for designing control fields in radical pair systems, with implications for experimental magnetoreception studies.

title: Construction Of near-Γ Multiple Chiral Exceptional Points In Momentum Space Of Photonic Crystal Slabs
authors: Jingyu Zhang, Yang Gao, Tianfu Ma, Wenjia Li, Weimin Ye And Jianlong Liu
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in optical systems have attracted considerable attention because of their nontrivial topological properties and unusual physical effects. Among them, scattering EPs are particularly appealing for describing chiral response through the scattering matrix. Photonic crystal slabs offer a versatile platform for studying chiral scattering EPs in momentum space, where their topological evolution can be conveniently accessed and engineered. In this work, a convenient approach is presented for achieving chiral scattering EPs near the Γ point by exploiting the topological evolution properties in the momentum space of photonic crystal slabs.
